rows.justification: Concrete object — speakers with music notes coming out, often boxy stereo shape. Iconic at A1.
Concrete classroom object — box with light beam projected onto wall/screen. Iconic at A1.
Concrete classroom item — large rectangle on a wall (blackboard/whiteboard) with chalk or pen. Iconic at A1.
Concrete object — rectangle with cross-frame, often with sun or curtains. Universal at A1.
Concrete object — tall rectangle with round handle. Iconic at A1.
Concrete object — table with drawers and a chair beside it. Iconic at A1.
Concrete object with iconic shape — two crossed blades + finger holes. A1 students recognize instantly.
Concrete object — long thin rectangle with cm markings. Iconic at A1.
Concrete object — flat rectangle with screen. A1 students see this every day.
Concrete object — iconic four-legged silhouette with back. A1 universal.
Concrete object — backpack with two straps, often with school logo. A1 universal.
Concrete object — long thin tube with cap and tip. Iconic at A1.
Concrete object — small notebook with lined pages. Iconic at A1.
Concrete object — small zippered bag with pens/pencils inside or sticking out. Iconic at A1.
Concrete object — long wooden stick with point and eraser. Iconic at A1.
Concrete object — small pink/white block. Iconic at A1 (note: British English for "eraser" — drawing reads regardless).
Concrete object — open book with pages or stack of books. Universal at A1.
Concrete object — curved band shape, often shown on a head. Risk of collapse to "hair". Backup: actor draws on a head profile.
Concrete object — two dark lenses joined by bridge + temples. Iconic at A1.
Concrete object — round crown with brim. Universal at A1.
Concrete clothing — long thin piece around neck with knot. Risk of collapse to "tie" generically. Backup: actor adds school-uniform shirt collar.
Concrete clothing — top with sleeves and collar. Iconic at A1.
Concrete clothing — pullover with long sleeves. Iconic at A1.
Concrete clothing — A-line shape from waist to knees. Iconic at A1.
Concrete clothing — sock-shaped tube, often striped. Iconic at A1.
Concrete object — side view of shoe with sole and laces. Iconic at A1.
Mime: hold imaginary object in both hands, extend forward to recipient with smile. Universal at A1 from many shared contexts.
Abstract concept. Drawing a clock reads as "clock". Best at A1: "what a clock shows — what time is it now?"
Abstract mental verb. Mime "finger up + nod" reads as "yes". Best at A1: "you know what something means — Do you understand?"
Mime: hold imaginary pen, scribble on imaginary paper, look pleased. Universal at A1.
Mime: smile big with hands together at chest, satisfied closed-eyes face, slight body sway. Reads at A1. Risk of collapse to "like".
Mime: hand cupped to ear, lean in, eyes closed concentrating. Universal at A1.
Mime: hands clasped at heart, eyes closed dreamily, big smile. Iconic at A1 from cartoon.
Abstract quantifier. Mime "more, more!" gesture is too vague. Best at A1: "a bigger number — I want more chocolate!"
Mime: hold open imaginary book, eyes scan side to side, turn page. Universal at A1.
Possessive pronoun. Mime fails. Best at A1: "it belongs to them — that is their bag, not ours".
Mime: raise hand, lean forward with curious face, mouth "?". Universal at A1 from classroom contexts.
Polysemous (street address; email). Drawing "envelope with words on it" reads as "letter". Best at A1: "where you live or your email name".
Mime: wave to imaginary person, big friendly smile, gesture toward them with open hand. Reads at A1 from greeting routines.
Mime: thumbs up, big smile, point at self, head nodding "yes good". Universal at A1.
Mime: extend hand for handshake to imaginary person, smile, mouth "hi". Universal at A1.
Time adverb. Mime "finger forward in time" too vague. Best at A1: "after that — first eat dinner, then watch TV".
Possessive pronoun. Mime "point at someone with this gesture" is too vague. Best at A1: "it belongs to you — is this your pen?"
Mime: hand cupped over eyes (binoculars-style), scan around dramatically. Universal at A1.
Conjunction. Best at A1: "one or the other — pizza or pasta?"
Iconic mime — bring imaginary food to mouth, chew, swallow with happy face. Universal at A1 from earliest gestures.
Mime: point forward, walk a few steps with arms swinging. Universal at A1.
Modal verb. Mime "point firmly + serious face" reads as "no"/"stop". Best at A1: "you have to do it — you must do your homework".
Question phrase. Mime "finger counting" reads as "count". Best at A1: "asking about the number — How many apples?"
Mime: angry frown, push away with disgust, shake head "no". Universal at A1.
Locative adverb. Mime "point at floor" is too vague (could be "this" or "ground"). Best at A1: "this place — Come here!"
Pronoun. No visual or mime. Best at A1: "a word for a thing or animal — the cat is small, it is nice".
Modal phrase (suggestion). Mime "beckon come" is too vague. Best at A1: "we do it together — Let's play football!"
Abstract time. Drawing "clock at 12 with moon" is plausible. Best at A1: "twelve o'clock at night — it's dark and everyone is asleep".
Possessive pronoun. Mime fails. Best at A1: "it belongs to us — this is our classroom".
Abstract preference adjective. Mime "point at thing + heart hands" collapses to "love". Best at A1: "the one you like the most — chocolate is my favourite".
Mime: search around with hand on brow, then suddenly point with delighted "aha!" face. Reads at A1. Risk of collapse to "look".
Polysemous (not dark; weight; lamp). Per definition the "pale colour" sense. Drawing "sun + bright objects" reads as "sun". Best at A1: "not dark — light blue is a colour".
Concrete person — small figure with shorter proportions, often with toy or backpack. Iconic at A1.
Mime: wipe imaginary surface with cloth, scrub with effort, then admire shine. Universal at A1.
Mime: push imaginary door shut, click handle, brush hands. Universal at A1.
Mime: turn imaginary door handle, push door open with both hands. Universal at A1.
Concrete object — framed rectangle with image inside (sun, person, etc.). Iconic at A1.
Mime: lower body onto an imaginary chair, settle in. Iconic at A1.
Mime: open mouth, point at lips, gesture talking with hand. Universal at A1.
Mime: rise from imaginary chair, push self up. Iconic at A1.
Mime: reach into imaginary bag, grasp object, pull it out, hold it up to show. Universal at A1.
Concrete configuration — classroom with rows of desks + students + teacher. Risk of collapse to "classroom". Backup: actor adds the multiple-students element.
Concrete object — trunk with branches and leaves. Iconic at A1.
Concrete animal — figure with curly tail, often hanging from branch with banana. Iconic at A1.
Concrete animal — colourful bird with curved beak, often on a perch. Iconic at A1.
Concrete animal — extremely long neck + spotted body. Iconic at A1.
Concrete vehicle — engine + carriages on tracks. Iconic at A1.
Concrete animal — black-and-white waddling bird. Iconic at A1.
Person defined by activity. Drawing "figure with map + group following" reads as "tourist". Best at A1: "a person who shows you around a place — the zoo guide showed us the animals".
Concrete animal — big cat with mane. Iconic at A1.
Spatial preposition. Mime "point to two things side-by-side" is plausible but vague. Best at A1: "very close to the side — the cat is next to the dog".
Preposition. Mime "point inside imaginary box" is too vague. Best at A1: "inside something — the cat is in the box".
Mime: stand behind imaginary object/person, pop head out, point "behind here". Reads at A1. Risk of collapse to "hide".
Mime: crouch as if ducking under imaginary table, point up to imaginary ceiling. Reads at A1. Risk of collapse to "low/hide".
Preposition. Mime "place hand on top of imaginary thing" is too vague. Best at A1: "on top of — the book is on the table".
Spatial preposition. Mime "stand in front of imaginary thing pointing back at it" is plausible but vague. Best at A1: "facing it, before it — the dog is in front of the door".
Concrete location — fenced area with various animals (lion, monkey, elephant). Iconic at A1.
Mime: gaze at imaginary object with hand on chest, "wow" face, sigh of admiration. Reads at A1. Risk of collapse to "nice/pretty".
Mime: arms spread very wide, eyes wide, "so big!" face. Universal at A1.
Question word. Mime "shrug + look around with question face" is too vague. Best at A1: "asking about place — Where is my pen?"
Mime: pinch fingers tiny, hands close together showing small, eyes squinted. Universal at A1.
Concrete person — taller figure compared to child. Risk of collapse to "person". Backup: actor draws an adult next to a smaller child for scale.
Preposition. Mime fails. Best at A1: "showing place — I am at school".
Mime: walk forward holding imaginary object, present it to imaginary person with smile. Universal at A1.
Conjunction. No visual. Best at A1: "shows a different idea — I like apples but not bananas".
Concrete animal — four legs + tail + floppy ears. Iconic at A1.
Concrete group — figures of mum, dad, kids, often in a row. Risk of collapse to "people". Backup: actor adds different ages/sizes.
Polysemous (no cost; not in prison; not busy). Per definition "no cost". Drawing "price tag with X through it + 0€" is plausible. Best at A1: "you do not pay — entry is free".
Concrete person — older woman, often with grey hair, glasses, smile. Iconic at A1.
Abstract collection. Drawing "figures together in a circle" reads as "friends". Best at A1: "some people together — a group of students".
Mime: hold hands far apart showing length, drag finger out a long way. Universal at A1.
Concrete object — small rectangle with text + perforated edge. Iconic at A1.
Mime: reach toward imaginary thing with grabbing hands, eager face, mouth "please". Universal at A1.
Preposition. No visual. Best at A1: "showing where someone comes — I am from Austria".
Abstract time-noun. Polysemous (year of life; school year). Drawing "calendar with 12 months" is plausible but vague. Best at A1: "twelve months — I am 11 years old".
Pronoun. No visual. Best at A1: "a word for a boy/man — He is my friend".
Pronoun. No visual. Best at A1: "a word for a girl/woman — She is my friend".
Mime: face imaginary person, mouth opens and closes with hand gestures, head bobs. Universal at A1.
Pronoun. No visual. Best at A1: "a word for more than one person — They are my friends".
Pronoun. Mime "point at self + others around" is plausible but specific. Best at A1: "me and other people — We are happy".
Preposition. No visual. Best at A1: "showing who gets it — This present is for you".
Mime: huge smile, jump up and down, arms in the air. Iconic at A1.
Mime: open imaginary door, gesture for someone to exit, watch them go. Reads at A1. Risk of collapse to "open".
Pronoun (object form). No visual. Best at A1: "me and other people — Mum gave us cake".
Concrete vehicle — boxy shape with four wheels. Iconic at A1.
Mime: throw arms up in relief, sigh deeply, look at imaginary watch. Reads at A1 from "finally!" contexts. Risk of collapse to "tired".
Mime: lean forward with raised eyebrow, hand on chin, "hmm?" face. Reads at A1. Risk of collapse to "confused".
Mime: extend hand to receive imaginary thing, peer at it with curious face. Reads at A1. Risk of collapse to "look".
Concrete object — round/oval grey shape on ground. Iconic at A1.
Concrete body part — drawing of hand with fingers labelled, or one finger pointing up. Iconic at A1.
Concrete body part — close-up of ear shape. Iconic at A1.
Concrete body part — face profile showing nose, or close-up. Iconic at A1.
Concrete body part — head with hair shown clearly. Iconic at A1.
Concrete body part — eye shape with iris and lashes. Iconic at A1.
Concrete body part — mouth open or closed in face profile. Iconic at A1.
Concrete physical feature — face with thick chin/cheek hair. Iconic at A1.
Concrete body part with directional specifier. Drawing "figure with arrow on right arm" reads. Risk of collapse to "arm". Backup: actor labels "R".
Mirror of right arm. Risk of collapse to "arm". Backup: actor labels "L".
Concrete body part — figure with arrow pointing to shoulder joint. Iconic at A1.
Concrete body part — figure with leg highlighted, or just a leg silhouette. Iconic at A1.
Concrete body part — outline of foot from side. Iconic at A1.
Concrete body part — two feet shown together. Plural form, but the drawing reads instantly. Same handling as "foot".
Concrete body part — single tooth shape. Iconic at A1.
Concrete body part — row of teeth, often in a smile. Iconic at A1.
Mime: stretch up tall, hand high above head. Universal at A1.
Polysemous (short height; short length). Mime "crouch low/show small height" reads as "short person". Risk of overlap with "small" — actor uses height-comparison gesture.
Function adverb. No visual. Best at A1: "too, as well — I like pizza, also pasta".
Mime: pose like celebrity for cameras, autograph signing, big confident smile, paparazzi gestures. Reads at A1 from media. Risk of collapse to "singer" or "actor".
Pronoun (object). No visual. Best at A1: "a word for a boy/man — I see him".
Possessive pronoun. No visual. Best at A1: "it belongs to a boy/man — that is his pen".
Concrete vehicle — large boat with sails or smokestacks on water. Iconic at A1.
Mime: flex bicep with proud face, lift imaginary heavy weight. Universal at A1.
Iconic visual — figure in uniform with hat at ship's wheel. Risk of collapse to "sailor". Backup: actor draws stripes on the cap.
Modal verb. Mime "hold something + point at self" collapses to "me"/"mine". Best at A1: "to own or have — I have got a dog".
Polysemous (pretty=nice-looking; pretty=quite). Per definition the "nice-looking" sense. Mime "hands frame face with smile" reads as "beautiful". Best at A1: "nice to look at — She is pretty".
Concrete colour — purple square or purple object (grape, flower). Iconic at A1.
Abstract time. Drawing "calendar with 7 days" is plausible but vague. Best at A1: "seven days — Monday to Sunday is one week".
Function adverb. Mime "circular gesture/repeat" is too vague. Best at A1: "one more time — Sing it again!"
Polysemous (return; body part; direction). Per definition the "return" sense. Mime "point backwards/turn around" is too vague. Best at A1: "to where you were — Come back!"
Mime: hold imaginary brush, dip in imaginary paint, brush onto imaginary canvas with artistic strokes. Universal at A1.
Family relation. Drawing "two girls together (one labelled sister)" is plausible. Best at A1: "a girl in your family — my sister is 8 years old".
Concrete person — small male figure, often with short hair + shorts. Iconic at A1.
Concrete person — small female figure, often with longer hair or dress. Iconic at A1.
Concrete person — adult male figure. Iconic at A1.
Concrete person — adult female figure. Iconic at A1.
Set phrase. Mime "point at imaginary girl + write name in air" is too narrative. Best at A1: "telling who a girl is — Her name is Anna".
Set phrase. Mime "point at imaginary boy + write name in air" is too narrative. Best at A1: "telling who a boy is — His name is Tom".
Mime: shiver, hug self, teeth chatter, blue lips face. Iconic at A1.
Mime: red face puffed cheeks, fists, stomp foot, frown. Iconic at A1.
Mime: hands to face, wide eyes, tremble, take steps back. Iconic at A1.
Mime: jump up and down, big smile, hands clapping, eager face. Universal at A1.
Mime: wipe forehead, fan self, fan-with-shirt motion, exhale loudly. Universal at A1.
Mime: head on hand, slouch, blank stare, sigh. Universal at A1.
Mime: pout, head down, slump shoulders, fake-cry rub eyes. Universal at A1.
Mime: hold stomach, mime eating motion, weak "feed me" face. Universal at A1 from many shared contexts.
Mime: bite nails, fidget feet, look around worriedly, jiggle leg. Reads at A1 from many shared school contexts.
Mime: yawn big, rub eyes, slump, mime falling asleep. Universal at A1.
Mime: chest out, hands on hips, beaming smile, point at imaginary medal. Reads at A1. Risk of collapse to "happy".
Concrete time of day — sunrise + bird + alarm clock. Risk of collapse to "sun". Backup: actor adds the "waking up" element.
Concrete time of day — clock at 12 + plate of food. Reads at A1. Risk of collapse to "food".
Abstract time. Drawing "sun high in sky after lunch" is plausible but vague. Best at A1: "after lunch, before evening — I do my homework in the afternoon".
Concrete time of day — sun setting + dinner table. Risk of collapse to "sunset".
Concrete time of day — moon + stars in dark sky. Iconic at A1.
Day name. Mime is too vague. Best at A1: "first day of the week — Monday is school day after the weekend".
Day name. Best at A1: "second day of the week — after Monday".
Day name. Best at A1: "third day of the week".
Day name. Best at A1: "fourth day of the week".
Day name. Best at A1: "fifth day of the week — last day of school".
Day name. Best at A1: "sixth day, weekend day".
Day name. Best at A1: "seventh day, the other weekend day".
Time/order preposition. Best at A1: "later than — after lunch, we go to the park".
Polysemous (24 hours; daytime). Drawing "sun" reads as "sun"/"day". Best at A1: "24 hours — Monday is one day".
Abstract noun. Drawing "finish line + arrow at end of road" is plausible but vague. Best at A1: "the last part — the end of the story".
Mime: laugh, dance, do silly action, big smile. Reads at A1. Risk of collapse to "happy".
Mime: shoo with both hands, point at imaginary door, frown. Universal at A1.
Abstract verb. No clean mime. Best at A1: "to take place — what happened?"
Concrete event — stage with curtain + audience watching. Polysemous (verb "to show"; the noun "TV show"). Backup: actor adds the audience-watching element.

rows.w: a day in the life of
rows.justification: Multi-word abstract phrase. No clean mime. Best at A1: "one normal day for a person — a day in the life of a teacher".
Mime: lay head on hands, eyes closed, snore softly. Universal at A1.
Mime: yawn while looking at imaginary watch showing 6am, sun just rising. Reads at A1. Risk of collapse to "morning".
Abstract noun. Mime fails. Best at A1: "the time when you are alive — my dog had a long, happy life".
Function adverb. Mime fails. Best at A1: "even now, continuing — Are you still here?"
Concrete object — open book with pictures inside. Risk of collapse to "book". Backup: actor adds the "speech bubble of fairy tale" element.
Time adverb. Mime "point at floor + serious face" is too vague. Best at A1: "this day, now — Today is Monday".
Mime: lean toward imaginary person with concerned face, hand on shoulder, mouth question. Reads at A1. Risk of collapse to "how are you".
Concrete object — exercise book at home with pen + "HOMEWORK" written. Iconic at A1.
Preposition with motion. Mime "walk forward into imaginary box" is plausible but reads as "in". Best at A1: "going inside — go into the room".
Mime: hands to cheeks with concerned face, head shake, "tut tut"-style worry. Reads at A1. Risk of collapse to "worried".
Concrete location — square with door + window + bed. Iconic at A1.
Mime: thumbs down, frown, push imaginary thing away with disgust. Reads at A1. Risk of collapse to "angry" or "hate".
Set imperative. Mime "finger wag + point at imaginary watch + serious face" is too vague. Best at A1: "telling someone to come on time".
Time adverb. Mime "point forward + sun rising" is too vague. Best at A1: "the day after today".
Concrete event — cake with candles + balloons + "HAPPY BIRTHDAY" sign. Iconic at A1.
Abstract relation. Drawing "two figures with arms around each other smiling" is plausible but vague. Best at A1: "a person you like — She is my best friend".
Set phrase. Mime "point at self + thumbs up" reads as "me good". Best at A1: "act how you really are — Don't pretend, be yourself".
Function phrase. Mime "shake head + point at one person only" is too vague. Best at A1: "not any other person — Only you, no one else".
Concrete object — narrow neck + wider body, often with cap. Iconic at A1.
Mime: someone takes imaginary object from you, you reach and grab it back, satisfied face. Reads at A1. Risk of collapse to "take".
Same as "angry" — mime: red face, fists, stomp. Risk of duplicate. Backup: actor uses milder version.
Mime: wave imaginary wand, "abracadabra" gesture, then jaw drops at imaginary trick. Reads at A1 from cartoon. Risk of collapse to "trick".
Mime: hold imaginary object, snap it in half with effort, look surprised at the pieces. Universal at A1.
Mime: yawn, walk to imaginary bed, lie down, close eyes. Universal at A1.
Conjunction. No visual. Best at A1: "for the reason that — I'm tired because I went to bed late".
Set phrase. Mime "point at self + smile + wave" is plausible. Best at A1: "saying who you are — Open the door, it's me".
Mime: hold out imaginary thing eagerly, gesture "go on" with encouraging face. Universal at A1.
Mime: open hands wide releasing imaginary object dramatically. Universal at A1.
Mime: arms up with confused face, look around in all directions, shrug. Reads at A1. Risk of collapse to "confused" or "where".
Mime: pretend to play keyboard with both hands, wiggle fingers on keys, head bobbing to music. Reads at A1. Risk of collapse to "piano".
Concrete instrument — long row of black-and-white keys. Iconic at A1.
Mime: hold imaginary microphone, mouth wide open singing, dramatic stage pose. Iconic at A1.
Mime: hold two imaginary drumsticks, hit imaginary drums fast with rhythm, head banging. Iconic at A1.
Concrete instrument — drum kit with snare + toms + cymbals. Iconic at A1.
Mime: hold curved imaginary saxophone with both hands, lips on mouthpiece, sway with jazz feeling. Reads at A1. Risk of collapse to "trumpet".
Concrete instrument — distinctive curved brass shape with bell at bottom. Iconic at A1.
Mime: hold imaginary guitar with neck up, strum with right hand, fingers on imaginary frets. Iconic at A1.
Concrete instrument — body + neck + tuning pegs, often with strings shown. Iconic at A1.
Specific relation. Drawing "two figures holding hands with heart above" reads as "love". Best at A1: "a boy who is your special friend — She has a boyfriend named Tom".
Possessive pronoun. No visual. Best at A1: "belonging to a thing or animal — the dog and its bone".
Mime: do many fun actions in sequence — kick imaginary ball, throw, dance, laugh. Reads at A1 as "playing". Polysemous (play music; play games) — actor uses the games sense to disambiguate.
Concrete event — stage with band + audience + speakers + lights. Iconic at A1.
Mime: dance with arms swaying, body moving to imaginary beat, big smile. Universal at A1.
Mime: pat imaginary friend on shoulder, gentle smile, wave hand calmly. Universal at A1.
Polysemous (work; task). Drawing "figure in different uniforms" reads as "worker". Best at A1: "work you do — my dad's job is in a shop".
Mime: "chef's kiss" with fingers, big satisfied smile, OK-sign with hand. Reads at A1. Risk of collapse to "good".
Mime: pretend to lift imaginary heavy box, hold it close to chest, walk a few steps. Universal at A1.
Mime: pretend to step up onto an imaginary box/chair, balance on it. Reads at A1.
Concrete body part — face with tongue sticking out. Iconic at A1.
Mime: extend index finger and gently poke imaginary thing/person. Universal at A1.
Mime: walk in place on imaginary surface (grass/sand) with exaggerated steps. Reads at A1. Risk of collapse to "walk".
Mime: wiggle hips/bottom side to side rapidly, or wiggle finger/eyebrows. Reads at A1 from many shared contexts.
Concrete object — cylindrical metal can (soda or food). Polysemous with modal "can" — but the noun reads instantly when drawn. Iconic at A1.
Mime: hold imaginary cup to mouth, tilt head back, big satisfied gulp. Universal at A1.
Concrete number — write "100" or "HUNDRED". Iconic at A1.
Idiomatic phrase. Mime "drink whole bottle without stopping + thumbs up" reads but vague. Best at A1: "all at one time, not stopping — I drank the juice in one go".
Mime: raised eyebrow, lean forward with surprised face, mouth "really?". Reads at A1. Risk of collapse to "surprised".
Mime: point clearly at self with both hands, wave, big smile. Reads at A1. Risk of collapse to "me" alone.
Abstract concept (money/business system). Drawing fails. Best at A1: "how money and business work in a country — Austria's economy is doing well".
Concrete location — building with red cross + ambulance + people in beds. Iconic at A1.
Mime: throw head back, hold belly, mouth "ha ha ha". Universal at A1.
Compound concept. Drawing "parent giving child coins" is plausible. Best at A1: "money your parents give you — I get 5 euros pocket money each week".
Concrete object — British banknote/coin with £ symbol. Risk of collapse to "money". Backup: actor adds £ symbol prominently.
Abstract financial concept. Drawing "arrow up + money" is too vague. Best at A1: "the money you make — the shop made a big profit".
Concrete location — large room with tables + kids eating + serving counter. Risk of collapse to "restaurant". Backup: actor adds the school-uniform element.
Concrete furniture — flat top with four legs. Iconic at A1.
Concrete person — figure pointing at board, often with book. Iconic at A1.
Family relation. Drawing "adult man with smile" reads as "man". Best at A1: "your mum's or dad's brother — my uncle gave me a present".
Mime: rub hands together with imaginary soap, scrub clothes/face, splash water. Universal at A1.
Function word (negation). Mime "shrug + empty hands" is too vague. Best at A1: "not anything — There is nothing in the box".
Mime: hand cupped to ear, lean forward, raised eyebrow asking "what?". Reads at A1. Risk of collapse to "listen".
Concrete location — skyline with tall buildings + cars. Iconic at A1.
Concrete location — trees + bench + grass. Iconic at A1.
Concrete location — road with houses + cars. Iconic at A1.
Concrete location — stalls with fruits/vegetables + people shopping. Iconic at A1.
Concrete location — building with "SUPER" sign + shopping carts + aisles. Iconic at A1.
Concrete feature — wavy line of water with banks + maybe a fish. Iconic at A1.
Concrete location — many trees clustered together. Iconic at A1.
Mime: stand at edge, jump forward with arms up, splash motion. Universal at A1.
Mime: pretend to push aside curtain, peer through glass with hand framing eyes. Universal at A1.
Mime: bend down, pick up imaginary object from floor, hold it up. Universal at A1.
Mime: pretend to sit on a high branch with feet dangling, look around. Reads at A1. Risk of collapse to "sit".

Mime: walk happily with arms swinging, look around at imaginary trees. Reads at A1. Risk of collapse to "walk".
Mime: grab imaginary rope/handle with both hands, lean back and pull hard. Universal at A1.
Mime: grab imaginary branches with hands, place feet on imaginary trunk, climb up with effort. Universal at A1.
Mime: stand up from imaginary desk, walk to imaginary door, wave goodbye. Reads at A1. Risk of collapse to "leave".
Mime: look at imaginary mirror, pose, fix hair, smile at reflection. Universal at A1.
Mime: reach hand up, pull self up using imaginary holds, alternating hands. Universal at A1.
Mime: bend knees, push off floor with arms up, big jump. Universal at A1.
Mime: wave goodbye, walk away from imaginary place. Reads at A1. Risk of collapse to "go".
Concrete object — oval/rectangle shape with reflection. Iconic at A1.
Mime: pretend to slide jacket onto arms, pull over head, button up. Universal at A1.

Mime: stand on imaginary winner's podium, hands raised in victory, mouth "I'm the best!". Reads at A1. Risk of collapse to "good".
Iconic visual — figure with magnifying glass + trench coat + hat. Recognizable at A1 from media.

Profession defined by an output (writing books). Drawing a person at a desk with a book reads as generic 'writer'. Best to explain: 'a person who writes books — the author of Harry Potter is JK Rowling'.
Abstract role/status. Mime 'pointing to a group, then to self' is too vague. Best: 'a person who is part of a group or club — I'm a member of the football team'.
Person in transit defined by their context (vehicle). Drawing a person on a bus reads as 'bus' or 'person'. Best: 'a person who is travelling on a bus or train — not the driver, the people who ride'.
Mime: stand tall, then slowly drop down with arms going underwater motion. Captures the gradual downward movement. Drawing a boat going under works but is slower.
Abstract — to stay alive after danger. Mime 'I made it!' gesture leans toward 'happy'. Best: 'you stayed alive after something bad — they survived the storm'.
Abstract adjective about attentiveness. Mime 'dropping things while not looking' collapses to 'clumsy'. Best: 'not paying attention to what you do — careless mistakes'.
Concrete object with iconic silhouette (rectangle with curved handle). Drawing reads instantly. Mime 'holding a bag' is too generic.
Set polite phrase. Mime 'hand to ear leaning forward' might fit the 'please repeat' sense but misses the 'sorry' sense. Best: 'a polite way to say sorry, or to ask someone to say it again'.
Iconic mime — sneaky walk, look around, grab something quickly, hide it. Highly readable at A2 from cartoon and film conventions.
Cartoon thief — striped shirt, mask, bag with $ — is a recognizable visual at A2. Show via tip-toe sneaking is also strong but reads as 'to sneak/steal'. Drawing nails the noun specifically.
Iconic location — globe with arrow at the top, snow, ice, polar bear. The image is well-known at this age. Explain works but the visual is faster.
Iconic location — globe with arrow at the bottom, penguins, ice. Visually distinct from North Pole because of penguins. Drawing wins.
Mime: holding nose, full-body recoil, exaggerated grimace. The disgust expression is universal. Drawing a frowny face is too mild.
Concrete location — door with an arrow pointing in, or a doorway with a person walking through. Drawing reads instantly. Show 'walking through a door' is shareable but slower.
Mime: extend a paper toward the teacher's desk with a small bow. The handover gesture is iconic in school contexts. Drawing fails (no single visual moment).
Iconic mime — hand up, palm out, fingers spread. Universally readable as 'stop/wait'. Drawing fails (no visual moment).
Mime: shoo someone away with annoyed face, or step back with palms out. Reads at A2. Risk: collapses to 'go away'. Backup with the 'stop bothering' framing.
Abstract anticipatory feeling. Mime 'excited, can't wait' lands close to 'excited'. Explain via 'feel happy about something that will happen — I'm looking forward to my birthday next week'.
Concrete configuration — a line of stick figures one behind the other. Highly recognizable. Show 'standing alone' lacks the line element.
Mime: stand in a line behind imaginary people, look forward patiently, sigh. The behaviour 'standing in line' is the verb. Drawing covers the noun better.
Iconic mime — raised hand swinging side to side. Universal at A2. The most natural Show item.
Abstract — calendar date associated with birth. Mime 'pointing at calendar then baby' is too vague. Best: 'the day you were born — like, my date of birth is 5 May 2014'.
Mime: index finger up, palm out, mouthing 'one moment'. Similar to 'Hold on!' but slightly more casual; the actor distinguishes with a slight tilt. Risk of collapse to 'wait'.
Abstract — reaching a target. Mime 'crossing a finish line with arms up' is plausible but reads as 'to win'. Explain to specify the effort element: 'you got what you wanted after working hard'.
Mime: throw head back, hold belly, exaggerated laughing motion. Universal at A2. Drawing a smiley face is too mild.
Concrete banknote — rectangle with face/numbers/value. Drawing reads as 'money/banknote'. Risk: 'note' is polysemous in English (musical note, written note). Drawing a euro/dollar bill disambiguates.
Iconic symbol — % drawable in two strokes. Math concept students see in school. Drawing nails it; explanation is also fine but slower.
Mime: stand at podium with imaginary notes, gesture broadly while mouthing words. Reads as 'giving a speech' at A2. Drawing a podium with figure also works.
Concrete location — raised platform with curtains, lights, sometimes a microphone. Drawing reads instantly. Show 'standing on something' is too generic.
Polysemous English phrasal verb (test; audition). Mime 'doing something experimentally' collapses to the activity itself. Best: 'test something to see if it works — let's try out the new game'.
Abstract verb of arrival. Mime 'walking and pointing forward' is too generic. Best: 'arrive at a place — how do you get to school every day?'
Iconic mime — arms angled up like wings, body leaning forward, sound effects optional. The plane-takeoff gesture is universal at A2.
Mime: pretend to step up onto a vehicle, ducking head as if entering a doorway. Reads as 'boarding'. Drawing a stairway to plane is slower.
Iconic mime — arms out wide like wings, slow horizontal motion. Universal at A2. Can be combined with 'back' direction by going one way then turning.
Mime: pretend to step down from a vehicle, ducking head, looking around upon arrival. Mirrors 'to get on'. Reads instantly.
Multi-word medical phrase. Miming 'sick at high altitude' is risky — collapses to 'sick' or 'tired'. Best: 'feeling ill because you are very high up in the mountains'.
Mime: arms outstretched then slowly lowering, feet touching down with a small bend. Mirror of 'to take off'. Universal at A2.
Abstract phrase about elapsed time. Mime 'looking at watch then waiting' is too generic. Best: 'how much time you need — it takes one hour to get there'.
Mime: open imaginary door, climb into seat, close door, fasten belt. Reads as 'entering vehicle' instantly.

Abstract transactional verb (paying to borrow). Mime 'handing money + getting keys' could work but reads as generic 'buy/exchange'. Best: 'pay money to use something for a short time, then give it back'.
Mime: open imaginary door, climb out, close door behind you. Mirrors 'to get into'. Universal at A2.
Iconic mime — hands gripping imaginary steering wheel, body bouncing slightly with 'motion'. Universal at A2.
Mime: shoulder a bag, wave goodbye, walk out a door with purpose. Reads as 'starting a journey'. Risk of collapse to 'leave' — actor emphasises the 'start' moment.
Abstract — sustained creative work. Mime 'typing on a laptop' collapses to 'to type' or 'to use a computer'. Best: 'spend time making something, like writing posts on a blog'.
Abstract metaphor (proximity to abstract concept). Mime 'reaching toward something' too vague. Best: 'come near to something — when you go camping, you get close to nature'.
Mime: pretend to set up a tent, crawl in, lie down with hands under head. Drawing a tent with a person also works. The mime reads as 'camping' specifically.
Abstract metaphorical use of 'escape' (avoid, not flee). Mime 'running into shade fanning self' is plausible but reads as 'hot'. Best to explain the avoidance sense.
Mime: step carefully across an imaginary line on the floor, looking down at imaginary water. Drawing a bridge with figure is also clear. Mime captures the act.
Phrasal verb specifying planned social meeting. Mime 'wave hello + hug' collapses to 'meet' alone. Best: 'see friends at a time you both planned — let's meet up at the park at three'.
Abstract change-of-state verb. No visual referent, no clean mime. Best: 'to start to be something — water becomes ice when it's cold'.
Mime: lean forward, raised eyebrow, hand cupping ear, eyes wide. Captures the inquisitive expression cleanly. Drawing fails (no single image). Universal at A2.
Abstract noun (a choice). Mime 'finger weighing two options then pointing at one' is plausible but ambiguous. Best: 'a choice you make — I made the decision to go to the party'.
Abstract noun, polysemous (event; accumulated knowledge). Nothing to draw or mime. Best: 'something that happens to you, or knowing how to do things from doing them many times'.
Mime: tip-toe through new territory, hand on brow scanning the horizon, peeking around corners. The exploratory gestures are evocative. Risk: collapses to 'looking'. Backup with 'new place' framing.
Concrete-enough to draw — a winding path with start and end, maybe a backpack. Show 'walking with a bag' is possible. Drawing a map-style trip captures the noun cleanly.
Adverbial phrase about transportation mode. Mime 'walking' collapses to 'to walk'. Best: 'walking, not using a car — I go to school on foot'.
Mime: clutch a body part, scrunched face, sharp inhale. Pain-face is universal at A2. Drawing fails (sad face is too mild).

Polysemous (extend an arm; arrive at). Mime 'stretching arm and fingers toward something just out of grasp' captures the physical sense cleanly. Risk of collapse to 'arrive' — the actor emphasises the stretch.
Mime: hand on imaginary tiller, lean into wind, look at sails above. Iconic boat-steering gesture. Drawing a sailboat is also clean but the action is what 'to sail' is.
Iconic visual — figure with backpack, rolling suitcase, map in hand. Drawing reads instantly. Show 'walking with a bag' is shareable but risks collapse to 'tourist'.
Mime: sit alone, hug knees, look around for someone, sad face. The body language is distinct from 'sad' or 'unhappy' — captures isolation.
Abstract negative-speech verb. Mime 'wagging finger with frown' collapses to 'angry' or 'no'. Best: 'say what is wrong with someone or something — the teacher criticised my essay'.
Iconic visual — figure with pith helmet, binoculars, map, jungle background. The cartoon-explorer image is recognizable at this age. Distinct from 'traveller' through the explorer-gear cliché.
Conjunction. No visual or mimable referent. Best: 'although — even though it was raining, we went outside'.
Concrete object — small cabin with sloped roof. Iconic and quick to sketch. Show 'kneeling in a small space' is too vague.
Abstract idiomatic verb (be discovered to be true in the end). Mime 'hands rotating then aha' fails. Best: 'in the end, you find out — it turned out he was right'.
Concrete-enough — remote forest/mountain landscape, no buildings. Drawing reads as 'wild nature'. Risk of collapse to 'forest'. Show fails (no human action).

Abstract verb of conduct. Polysemous (act in general; behave well). Mime 'sitting still nicely' collapses to 'good'. Best: 'to act in a certain way — kids behave better when their parents are watching'.
Discourse phrase summarizing. No visual or mime. Best: 'when you think about everything together — all in all, it was a good trip'.
Mime: eyes wide, sit up suddenly, point to open eyes. Reads as 'awake/alert'. Drawing eyes open is also possible. Show wins for the alertness energy.
Adverb of degree (note: 'quite' sense, not the looks sense). High-collision risk if students try Show or Draw — they'd act 'beautiful'. Must explain the moderating-adverb meaning explicitly.
Discourse marker showing regret. Mime 'shrug + sad face' collapses to 'sad' or 'sorry'. Best: 'you say this when you are sorry about something — unfortunately, the shop was closed'.
Abstract noun for the moment of leaving. Drawing an airport departures board is plausible but slow. Best: 'when a plane or train leaves — the departure is at 7am'.
Iconic visual — plane in sky with clouds, or a contrail. Drawing reads instantly. Show 'flying' captures the verb 'to fly' rather than the noun.
Mime: phone to ear with finger raised, gesture writing in a calendar. Reads at A2 from restaurant/booking contexts. Risk of collapse to 'on the phone'.
Abstract verb of observation. Mime 'finger to head, raised eyebrow' too vague. Best: 'to notice or pay attention to something — please note that the meeting is on Tuesday'.
Mime: hammering, turning a screwdriver, frustrated peering at imaginary broken object then nodding satisfied. The repair gestures are iconic and varied.
Mime: tongue out, fan self, mime drinking from cup, gasp. Universally readable at A2 — even readable cross-language.
Abstract negative adjective. Mime 'big NO with hands crossed' collapses to 'no'. Best: 'cannot happen, no way — it's impossible to walk to the moon'.
Time adverb. No visual referent. Mime 'pointing back over shoulder' is too vague. Best: 'a short time ago — I saw him recently, last week I think'.
Mime: spin in confusion, hold up imaginary phone with poor signal, scratch head, look around. The lost-in-place body language is iconic at this age.
Abstract gradual-acquaintance verb. Mime 'shake hand then time gesture' collapses to 'to meet'. Best: 'learn more about a person or place over time'.
Iconic mime — hand on heart, raised right hand like an oath, serious face, sometimes pinky-promise gesture. Universal at A2.
Abstract verb of suggestion. Mime 'thumbs up + point at something' collapses to 'good'. Best: 'tell someone something is good and they should try it — I recommend the chocolate cake'.
Iconic visual — skull-and-crossbones, or a colourful frog/snake with warning markings. Drawing reads instantly. Show 'falling sick' is risky.
Mime: snarl, fists clenched, threatening lean-forward stance. The body language is universal at A2. Drawing a snarling face is reductive.
Iconic — yellow warning triangle with exclamation mark, or a cliff with arrow. Drawing reads as 'warning'. Show 'fearful step back' collapses to 'scared'.
Iconic visual — skull symbol or a snake. Drawing nails it. Show 'dramatic collapse' is too theatrical for the room. Risk of overlap with 'poisonous' — actor adds a knife/sword to disambiguate.
Mime: walk slowly with a straight back, head held high, hand-trail behind. The 'runway model' gesture lands at A2. Drawing a fancy dress collapses to 'dress'.
Abstract intensifier adjective. Mime 'jaw drops, hand to chest' collapses to 'shocked' or 'surprised'. Best: 'extremely beautiful — like, the view from the mountain was stunning'.
Mime: hands cupped on cheeks, exaggerated 'aww' face, looking at imaginary kitten/baby. Reads at A2 from many shared cultural references. Risk of collapse to 'small/baby'.
Mime: stroke imaginary soft fur, then bring hands to face cooing. Captures the texture sense. Drawing a fluffy animal silhouette collapses to the animal itself rather than the texture.
Mime: hug an imaginary teddy bear, snuggle face into it, contented sigh. The hugging gesture is iconic at A2.
Concrete — small bear/lion next to a bigger one for scale. The 'baby animal' element is the key. Drawing reads instantly.
Iconic mime — crossed fingers held up, thumbs-up, big encouraging smile. Universal at A2.
Iconic visual — large white bear on ice, sometimes near water. Drawing reads instantly. Show 'walking like a bear' is generic.

Similar to 'cute' — hands cupped on cheeks, melting expression. The 'aww' gesture with maximum exaggeration reads as 'adorable' specifically. Risk of overlap with 'cute' — backup with a baby-animal frame.
Mime: open mouth wide, snap teeth shut, then point to a body part. Reads as 'a bite' (the noun). Drawing teeth marks is also possible. Show is more visceral.
Abstract causation verb. Mime 'this leads to that' is too vague. Best: 'to make something happen, usually bad — the rain caused the flood'.

Iconic visual — bottle with skull-and-crossbones label. Drawing reads instantly. Risk of overlap with 'poisonous' — actor distinguishes by drawing the bottle (noun) vs the warning symbol alone (adjective).
Specific disease, no shared visual at A2 (foaming-mouth dog might land for some, mislead others). Best: 'a very dangerous illness from animal bites — dogs can have rabies'.
Concrete animal — torpedo body, flippers, whiskered face. Iconic and quick to sketch. Drawing reads instantly.
Concrete animal with iconic curved neck. Drawing reads instantly. Show 'graceful neck stretch' is plausible but slow.
Mime: hold imaginary apple/sandwich, take a big bite, tear off a chunk with teeth. The action is visceral and clear at A2.
Concrete animal — long body, four legs, tail, often on a rock. Iconic shape. Show 'crawling on hands and knees' is generic.
Mime: shoo with both hands, run forward at imaginary creature, wave arms threateningly. Captures the 'making them leave' element.
Mime: pouty face, hands on hips, exaggerated grumbling sounds, finger-wagging at someone. The body language is iconic in family/school contexts.

Abstract noun for body damage. Drawing a bandage collapses to 'plaster'. Mime 'limping with bandaged arm' reads as 'hurt'. Best: 'damage to a part of your body — she had an injury and went to hospital'.
Mime: bend knees, grasp an imaginary heavy box, straighten legs while raising it up with effort. Universal weightlifting/box-lifting gesture.
Mime: grab an imaginary high handle (like a bus stop cord or window blind) with both hands, pull straight down. Clear directional gesture.
Abstract verb (receive; agree to). Mime 'reach out and take' collapses to 'to take'. Best: 'say yes to something or take what is given — she accepted the gift'.
Time adverb. Mime 'snap fingers + go!' is plausible but ambiguous. Best: 'right now, no waiting — come here immediately!'
Multi-word complex idiom. Mime 'shake head while wagging finger' reads as 'no'. Best: 'tell someone NOT to do something — the doctor advised her against eating sugar'.
Mime: clutch arm, exaggerated dripping motion with shocked face, look at hand turned red. Visceral and reads at A2 from many film references.
Abstract concept. Drawing a tombstone is morbid for the classroom; mime 'collapse and lie still' is theatrical and possibly upsetting. Best handled in words: 'when a person or animal stops living'.
Mime: stand in front of someone with arms out blocking, fists raised, shield-like posture. The protective stance reads cleanly.
Multi-word abstract verb of confusion. Mime 'looking at A then B with confused face' collapses to 'confused'. Best: 'think one thing is something else — I mistook salt for sugar'.
Abstract statistical phrase. No visual or mime. Best: 'the usual amount — on average, kids sleep nine hours a night'.
Iconic visual — figure with mask, fins, oxygen tank, bubbles rising. Highly recognizable at this age. Drawing reads instantly.
Concept easiest shown with examples — sketch a circle, square, triangle, star side-by-side. Mime 'tracing shapes in the air' is plausible but vague. Drawing wins.
Abstract verb of belief/assumption. Mime 'finger to chin, raise eyebrow, shrug' is too vague (could be 'think'). Best: 'think something is probably true — I suppose he forgot'.
Abstract idiom (be careful; look after). Mime 'finger wag with cautious face' is ambiguous. Best: 'be careful or look after — take care when you cross the road'.
Abstract role-noun for someone harmed. Mime 'hurt person looking sad' collapses to 'sad/hurt'. Best: 'a person who is hurt or harmed by something — there were three victims of the accident'.
Mime: gesture wildly, mouth words, signal with hands, point ears. The 'multi-channel signalling' captures the breadth. Risk of collapse to 'to talk'.
Concrete configuration — rows of seats with people facing a stage. Drawing reads as 'crowd watching'. Mime 'sitting and clapping' captures only one moment.
Iconic visual — trees, sky, river, animals. Drawing a nature panorama with the Earth in background reads as 'nature/environment'. Show fails (no clear action). Risk of collapse to 'nature'.
Iconic mime — palms out, push-away gesture, sharp head-shake, frown. The 'don't touch' message is universal at A2.
Abstract communicative verb. Mime 'lean in and tell secret' collapses to 'to tell' or 'to whisper'. Best: 'tell someone about something important — please inform the teacher'.
Mime: pretend to push someone behind bars, then turn an imaginary key with finality, then pocket the key. The two-stage gesture (lock + pocket) is unmistakable.
Profession defined by what they do. Drawing a person at a podium reads as 'speaker'. Best: 'someone whose job is to work in the government and make laws — like the chancellor or the president'.

Abstract state of bad luck. Mime 'sad face after dropping something' collapses to 'sad' or 'clumsy'. Best: 'when bad things keep happening to you — I'm so unlucky today, I lost my keys and missed the bus'.
Iconic mime — close eyes, hands together (or blow on candles, or hold a coin and toss it into a fountain). Universal at A2 from birthday and shooting-star contexts.

Abstract verb of wanting. Closely related to 'make a wish' — actor risks repetition. Best in words: 'really want something — I wish for a new bike'. Saves the iconic candle-blow mime for 'make a wish'.
Abstract idiom about causing fortune. Mime 'crossed fingers + something happens' is too vague. Best: 'cause good or bad things to happen — black cats are said to bring bad luck'.
Abstract idiom (a wish becoming real). Mime 'wish then suddenly aha!' is hard to read. Best: 'when a wish or a dream really happens — my wish came true'.
Mime: hunched ghost-walk, fingers wiggling, exaggerated wide eyes, 'oooooh' mouth. The Halloween-ghost gesture is universal at A2.
Abstract chance state. Mime 'fingers crossed + smile' collapses to 'lucky'. Best: 'when good or bad things happen to you — she had good luck and won the lottery'.
Multi-word abstract phrase about belief. Nothing visual or mimable. Best: 'thinking that old stories about luck are true — like, never walk under a ladder'.
Concrete object — round clock with two bells on top, hands showing time. Highly iconic at A2. Drawing reads instantly. Show 'waking up startled' is risky.
Set polite question. Mime 'shrug with hopeful face' is ambiguous. Best: 'a way to ask if someone got what they wanted — Did you find your keys? Any luck?'

Preposition. Mime 'point to one thing then to next-to-it' is plausible but ambiguous with 'next to'. Best: 'next to, at the side of — the cat is beside the dog'. Drawing two stick figures side-by-side is also fine but slow.
Set polite question. Nothing to draw or mime. Best: 'a polite way to ask if something is OK — Do you mind if I open the window?'
Mime: villain stance, evil grin, hand-rubbing gesture, raised eyebrow. The cartoon-villain pose is recognizable at A2. Risk of collapse to 'bad' — actor exaggerates the maniacal element.
Mime: laugh, point at someone with finger, big smile, shake head. Reads as 'just kidding!'. Risk: collapse to 'laughing'. Backup with finger-point.
Mime: turn head away pointedly, look the other direction with arms crossed. Body language is unmistakable at A2 from playground contexts.
Mime: lean back with hands on belly, contented sigh, small nod. Reads as 'happy/content'. Risk of collapse to 'happy' — actor adds the post-meal lean-back.
Mime: open mouth wide, hands to face, eyes shut, exaggerated scream gesture (no actual sound). Universal at A2 from horror-film conventions.
Concrete object — long zipped bag with a head sticking out, often striped. Drawing reads instantly. Show 'lying in a bag' is plausible but slow.
Iconic visual — wavy ghost outline with hollow eyes. Drawing reads as 'ghost' specifically. Show 'floating with arms out' is plausible but reads as generic 'ghost'.
Abstract belief noun. Drawing fails (which superstition?). Best: 'an old belief about luck — like, breaking a mirror brings seven years of bad luck'.
Abstract verb of pulling-in. Mime 'beckoning with both hands' collapses to 'come here'. Best: 'make someone or something come closer — flowers attract bees'.
Mime: open imaginary door, step over a threshold, look around the new room. Reads as 'going into' instantly.
Mime: pretend to snip imaginary scissors around your own head, look in mirror, ruffle hair. Reads at A2. Drawing a salon scene also works but is slow.
Abstract adjective about clarity. Mime 'eye-roll with palms up' collapses to 'frustrated/annoyed'. Best: 'easy to see or understand — it's obvious he's tired, he keeps yawning'.
Abstract adjective. Drawing 'old-fashioned thing' is too specific (which tradition?). Best: 'done the same way for a long time — wearing dirndl is a traditional Austrian costume'.
Mime: sneaky face, hide something behind back, point one way while going the other. The 'gotcha' gesture reads at A2 from cartoon contexts.
Abstract adjective. Closely related to 'to be unlucky'. Best in words to avoid duplicate mime: 'having or bringing bad luck — Friday the 13th is unlucky for some people'.
Mime: pucker lips, hands cupped to mouth, head bobbing as if making a tune. The whistling shape is recognizable. Universal at A2.
Concrete physical feature — thin jagged line on a wall, ground, or window. Drawing reads as 'crack'. Show 'pretending to step over a line' is plausible but vague.

Concrete bird, but distinguishing from generic 'bird' visually is hard. Drawing a cuckoo clock with the bird popping out is the iconic A2 reference. Show 'bird call sound' is forbidden (no sound effects in classroom mime).
Concrete urban feature — rectangular slabs next to a road with cars. Drawing reads instantly. Show 'walking on a sidewalk' is too generic.
Mime: count imaginary money fanned out, point to imaginary diamond ring, swagger. The 'wealthy' gestures are caricatured at A2. Risk of collapse to 'money'.
Mime: shake hands of an imaginary bottle of juice up and down vigorously, then hold it still. Universal at A2.
Abstract adjective. Closely related to 'superstition'. Best: 'someone who believes in old luck stories — my grandma is superstitious, she never walks under ladders'.
Mime: sneeze, blow nose, shiver, sniffle, hold throat. The cold-symptoms package reads at A2. Risk of collapse to 'sick'.
Concrete object — small brush with handle and bristles. Iconic and quick to sketch. Show 'brushing teeth' captures the verb 'to brush' rather than the noun.
Abstract verb of organizing. Mime 'moving things into order' collapses to 'tidy up'. Best: 'plan something — let's arrange a meeting on Friday'.
Set discourse phrase. Mime 'firm head-nod with confident face' is ambiguous (could be 'yes' or 'agree'). Best: 'a way to say you are certain — I'm sure he will come'.
Concrete object — four-leaf clover, horseshoe, rabbit's foot, or similar trinket. Drawing one of the iconic charms reads as 'good luck object'. Show fails (no action).
Concrete substance — salt shaker with white grains, or a dish of salt. Iconic and quick to sketch. Drawing reads instantly.
Discourse adverb. Mime 'serious face + finger up' collapses to 'serious' as adjective. Best: 'really, no joke — seriously, you should try this cake'.
Concrete structure — arch over water with rails. Iconic silhouette. Drawing reads instantly. Show 'walking across' captures the verb 'to cross'.
Concrete feature — long wavy line with banks, possibly a fish. Drawing reads as 'water/river'. Show fails (no clear action).
Concrete location — building with paintings hung on walls, figures looking up at them. Reads as 'gallery'. Risk of collapse to 'museum'. Backup: add a frame around a painting.
Concrete urban feature — open area with buildings around it, often a fountain or statue in middle. Polysemous (also the shape) so the actor draws benches/people to disambiguate from the geometry.
Concrete outdoor area — trees, grass, benches, paths. Iconic cluster of features. Drawing reads as 'park'.
Concrete structure — tall narrow building, often with windows up the sides. Iconic silhouette. Drawing reads instantly.
Abstract administrative division. Drawing 'a bunch of buildings' reads as 'town'. Best: 'an area of a city — Vienna has 23 districts'.
Concrete structure — rectangle with windows, door, roof. Most generic 'building' silhouette reads instantly. Show fails (no action).
Concrete urban feature — road with houses on each side, sometimes cars. Drawing reads instantly. Mime 'walking down a road' is too generic.
Concrete location — building with sign and shop window with goods inside. Drawing reads instantly. Show 'buying something' captures the verb.
Concrete large building with many shops inside, often labelled. Drawing reads as 'mall'. Risk of overlap with 'shop' — actor adds multiple smaller shops within a larger frame.
Concrete location — oval/round building with rows of seats, sometimes a pitch in middle. Drawing reads as 'sports stadium' instantly.
Mime: pretend something is on fire (waving fire-fingers around an imaginary house), then collapse it down with both hands. The fire + collapse reads at A2. Risk of collapse to 'fire'.

Abstract noun (a group of items). Drawing 'lots of one type of thing' reads as the items themselves rather than the noun 'collection'. Best: 'lots of things you have gathered — my brother has a collection of football cards'.
Abstract institution. Drawing a building with a flag is too generic. Best: 'the people who run a country — the government makes the laws'.
Iconic building — Big Ben tower next to a long Gothic building on the Thames. Recognizable from postcards and travel pictures. Drawing reads instantly for kids who've seen any London image.
Function phrase about timing. Mime 'pointing forward in time' is too vague. Best: 'before something happens — book the ticket in advance, two weeks before'.
Iconic mime — hold imaginary camera up to face, finger to click button, click sound (or just 'click' mouth shape). Universal at A2.

Polysemous in English (verb 'to play' vs noun 'theatre play'). Mime 'reading from a script on a stage' is plausible but reads as 'acting' or 'theatre'. Best to explain to disambiguate from the verb sense.
Iconic location — building with bars on windows, possibly a person behind bars. Drawing reads instantly. Risk: similar to 'jail' — but A2 students generally know prison from media.
Mime: bend down, grasp imaginary box, lift it up overhead with effort. The 'lifting upward' gesture reads as 'raise' specifically (vs 'lift' which can be just up to chest).
Concrete bird — black, large, often perched on a branch or roof. Risk of collapse to 'crow' or 'bird'. Show 'flapping arms like a bird' is too generic.
Mime: stroll casually with arms swinging, look around as if enjoying the view. The leisurely body language captures 'walk for pleasure' specifically.
Concrete location — building with marquee, columns, posters of plays, curtain in window. Iconic silhouette. Drawing reads as 'theatre'.
Abstract — what you can see from a place. Drawing 'a panoramic landscape from a window' reads as the landscape itself. Best: 'what you can see from a place — the view from the mountain is amazing'.

Person defined by context (visiting somewhere). Drawing 'a person knocking on a door' reads as 'guest' or 'arriving'. Best: 'a person who comes to see a place or another person — we had visitors at our house yesterday'.
Abstract intensifier adjective. Mime 'jaw drop with excited eyes' collapses to 'exciting'. Best: 'very exciting and a bit scary — the rollercoaster was thrilling'.
Function adverb (≈). Mime 'wobble hand back and forth' is too vague. Best: 'close to a number but not exact — there are approximately 30 students in our class'.
Mime: hand to mouth, exaggerated cough motion (no sound), repeat. The cough gesture is universal and visceral at A2.

Abstract negative-trait adjective. Mime 'evil grin while pretending to hurt something' is theatrical and possibly upsetting. Best: 'making others suffer on purpose — it's cruel to be mean to animals'.
Mime: pick up imaginary glass, turn it upside down, shake it, sad face. The 'nothing inside' gesture lands at A2. Drawing an empty rectangle is also possible. Show wins for the action.
Mime: hand to forehead with concerned face, shiver, sweat-wipe. The illness body language reads as 'sick' but the forehead-touch is the 'fever' specifier. Risk of collapse to 'sick'.

Abstract communicative verb. Mime 'speaking into microphone like a news anchor' is plausible but reads as 'newsreader'. Best: 'tell someone about something — please report any problems to the teacher'.
Concrete narrow way — winding line through grass or trees. Drawing reads as 'path'. Show 'walking carefully' is generic.
Abstract intensifier adjective. Mime 'jaw drop, hand to chest' collapses to 'wow' or 'shocked'. Best: 'very impressive and beautiful — the fireworks were spectacular'.
Compound abstract noun (place that draws tourists). Drawing 'famous landmark' is too unspecific (which one?). Best: 'a famous place tourists visit — the Eiffel Tower is a tourist attraction'.
Abstract verb of undergoing. Mime 'looking around amazed' collapses to 'amazed'. Best: 'see, feel, or do something — I experienced an earthquake last summer'.
Iconic visual — many cars on a road, possibly with a traffic light. Drawing reads as 'busy road' instantly. Show 'driving in jam' is plausible but slow.
Abstract compound adjective. Drawing 'flags from many countries' is too specific. Best: 'with people from many countries and cultures — Vienna is a multicultural city'.
Concrete document — paper with text and a signature line at the bottom, often with a pen. Drawing reads as 'document/agreement'. Risk of collapse to 'paper'. Backup: add a handshake icon below.
Mime: walk with confident posture, point forward, beckon others to follow with arm waves. The leadership stance reads at A2. Risk of collapse to 'walk forward'.
Concrete substance — sugar bowl with cubes, or a sugar packet. Iconic. Drawing reads instantly.
Mime: do work motions (typing, hammering), then receive imaginary money with satisfied face. The work-then-payment two-stage gesture reads as 'earning'. Risk of collapse to 'work' or 'money'.
Abstract verb of accumulating money for a goal. Mime 'putting coins in a piggybank one by one' reads at A2 but slow. Best: 'keep money for later to buy something — I'm saving up for a new bike'.
Mime: hold imaginary pen, swirl signature on imaginary paper with flourish. Universal at A2.

Idiomatic verb about ending a friendship through conflict. Mime 'turn back angrily on someone' collapses to 'angry'. Best: 'have a big argument and stop being friendly — I fell out with my best friend last week'.
Mime: stomp angrily, slam an imaginary door, leave with face like thunder. The angry-departure body language is iconic at this age (siblings, parents). Reads as 'storming out' specifically.
Idiom about ending a romantic relationship. Mime 'point at heart, then break it in half with hands' reads at A2 from media but is potentially awkward in classroom. Best in words for safety.

rows.g: sich um seine eigenen Angelegenheiten kümmern
rows.justification: Idiomatic phrase. Mime 'point to chest, then shoo away' is too vague. Best: 'don't ask about things that are not about you — Mind your own business!'

Mime: shake hands with imaginary person, hug, big smile of relief. The reconciliation gesture reads at A2. Risk of collapse to 'to hug' or 'to be friends'. Backup: actor first does an angry pose, then makes up.

rows.w: to get on well with sb.
rows.justification: Idiomatic phrase about good rapport. Mime 'two friends laughing together' collapses to 'friends'. Best: 'have a good friendly connection — I get on well with my cousin'.
Set discourse phrase. Mime 'shrug + look away' is too vague. Best: 'a way to say it's not your problem — what they do is none of my business'.
Mime: point at someone while laughing meanly with hand over mouth. Captures the mocking element. Risk of collapse to 'to laugh' — the pointing-and-mockery is the specifier.
Idiomatic decision-making phrase. Mime 'finger taps temple then aha!' is plausible but vague. Best: 'decide after thinking — I made up my mind to study harder'.
Mime: imitate someone in an exaggerated mocking way, point and laugh. Reads at A2 from playground contexts. Risk of overlap with 'to laugh at' — actor adds the imitation element.

In context = changing residence (note: NOT generic 'move' = 'to walk'). Mime: pick up imaginary boxes, load into truck, wave goodbye to a house. The 'house move' gesture reads at A2 but is not the only sense of 'move' — backup with the suitcase context.
Concrete object — stuffed teddy bear or similar with smile and floppy limbs. Iconic at A2. Drawing reads instantly.

Idiomatic phrasal verb (intervene). Mime 'literally step into a fight to break it up' reads at A2 from playground contexts. Risk of collapse to 'walk in'. Backup: explain — 'help when there's a problem'.

Abstract noun. Drawing 'two figures connected by a heart' is too narrow (it can be friendship, family, business). Best: 'how two people feel about and behave towards each other — my relationship with my brother is good'.
Abstract verb of possession. Mime 'point at something then to self' is too vague. Best: 'have something that is yours — my parents own a car'.
Abstract time-period noun. Drawing 'baby/kid pictures' reads as 'baby' or 'kid'. Best: 'the time when you are a child — my childhood was happy, we lived in the countryside'.
Concrete jewellery item. Iconic — small loop or stud near an ear in profile sketch. Drawing reads instantly.
Mime: glare angrily at someone with crossed arms, look at what they have, sulk. Reads at A2 from cartoon contexts. Risk of collapse to 'angry'.
Mime: zip imaginary lips closed, finger to mouth (shh!), look around to make sure no one heard. The 'don't tell' gesture is iconic. Risk: reads as 'be quiet'. Backup: lean in conspiratorially first.
Concrete document — paper with question marks, checkboxes, lines for answers. Drawing reads as 'survey/form'. Risk of collapse to 'paper'. Backup: add multiple checkboxes and a question mark.
Mime: stand tall, frown, wag finger at imaginary kid, mouthing angry words. The teacher/parent scolding gesture is iconic at this age.
Abstract verb (find an answer). Mime 'puzzle pieces clicking together + aha!' reads at A2 from cartoon contexts. Risk: collapses to 'puzzle'. Backup explain: 'find the answer to a problem'.
Abstract emotional adjective. Mime 'hands to heart at someone' collapses to 'love'. Best: 'loved very much — my beloved grandmother gave me this ring'.
Negative locative pronoun. Mime 'searching everywhere then shrug' is too vague. Best: 'not in any place — I looked but my keys were nowhere'.
Concrete document — bound pages with character names and dialogue lines. Drawing reads as 'play/film script'. Risk of collapse to 'book' — actor adds 'CHARACTER:' on lines.
Mime: pretend to push something heavy with strained face, sweat-wipe, exaggerated effort. Reads at A2 as 'work hard'. Risk: collapses to 'to push' or 'to work'. Backup with frustrated face.
Mime: tell something with shifty eyes, fingers crossed behind back, then reveal the crossed fingers. The 'crossed fingers' is the iconic A2 cue for lying. Risk: ambiguous without the reveal.
Abstract verb (confess to something). Mime 'shoulder slump, hand up, mouthing yes' is too vague. Best: 'say something is true, especially something bad — he admitted he broke the window'.
Specific abstract crime. Hard to mime safely in classroom (threatening). Best: 'force someone to do what you want by saying you'll tell their secret — bad people sometimes blackmail'.
Mime: trip over imaginary feet, drop imaginary objects, wobble, knock things over with apologetic face. The 'I keep messing up' body language reads instantly at A2.
Abstract trait. Mime 'hand on heart, sincere face' reads at A2 but risks collapse to 'promise' or 'sincere'. Best: 'always tells the truth — she's an honest person, she never lies'.
Concrete configuration — stack of objects (books, plates, clothes) tall and tilting. Iconic visual. Show 'stacking with hands' is plausible but the noun 'pile' is best as a drawn image.
Concrete physical feature — red dots on skin (arm or face). Drawing reads as 'spots on skin'. Risk of collapse to 'spots' — actor adds an itching mime in margin if needed.
Mime: hold stomach, pale face, wobble unsteadily, hand to forehead. Reads as 'sick'. Risk of overlap with other illness vocab — actor avoids fever-specific gestures (forehead) to avoid 'fever' guess.
Abstract creative verb. Mime 'finger to head, then point to imaginary new thing with aha!' is plausible but reads as 'idea'. Best: 'create something completely new — Edison invented the light bulb'.
Mime: pretend to mix beakers like a scientist, watch reaction with curious face, jot notes. The lab-scientist gesture reads at A2. Risk of collapse to 'science' or 'mix'.
Abstract verb of betterment. Mime 'wave thumbs from low to high' is too vague. Best: 'make something better — I want to improve my English by reading more'.
Mime: walk forward, then suddenly stop and point with shocked-delighted face at imaginary find. Reads as 'find/aha!' at A2. Risk of collapse to 'find' — actor adds the 'first time' gesture.
Idiomatic phrasal verb (figure out). Polysemous (also = exercise). Mime 'finger taps temple then aha!' is plausible but generic. Best: 'find the answer by thinking — I worked out the maths problem'.

Mime: hold imaginary pencil, sketch lines on imaginary paper while standing back to admire. The 'sketching plans' gesture reads as 'design' or 'draw'. Risk: collapse to 'draw'. Backup: actor adds measuring/considering gesture.

Polysemous English phrasal verb. Mime 'doing something experimentally' collapses to the activity itself. Best: 'test something to see if it works — let's try out the new game'. (Same call as Unit 2 — verb appears twice in MORE 3.)
Abstract verb of mass-making. Mime 'factory line motions' collapses to 'work' or 'machine'. Best: 'make something in large amounts — the factory produces 1,000 cars a day'.
Concrete food — wavy strips of pink and white meat. Iconic and quick to sketch. Drawing reads instantly.
Mime: hang imaginary garlands, place imaginary flowers, step back to admire. The decorating gesture is iconic at A2 from holiday contexts.

Polysemous English (plate; prepared food). The 'food/meal' sense is meant here. Drawing 'plate of food' collapses to 'plate' or specific food. Best: 'food prepared in a particular way — chocolate cake is my favourite dish'.
Abstract substance noun. Polysemous (also adjective 'fat = overweight'). Drawing 'oily liquid in a pan' is plausible but reads as 'oil'. Best: 'the oily part in food — bacon has a lot of fat in it'.
Abstract noun (something newly created). Drawing 'a generic gadget' is too unspecific. Best: 'something new someone created — the telephone was an important invention'.
Concrete configuration — many heads/figures packed together, often at a concert or event. Iconic visual. Drawing reads as 'lots of people' instantly.

Abstract physics noun (flow of electricity). Polysemous in English (also water current; also adjective 'current = present'). Drawing 'a wire with sparks' is too unspecific. Best: 'electricity flowing in a wire — current makes the lights work'.
Abstract verb of gradual creation. Mime 'tiny seedling growing big' is plausible but reads as 'grow'. Best: 'create something new over time — they developed a new app for the school'.
Compound technical adjective/noun. Drawing 'a motor with a lightning bolt' is plausible but vague. Best: 'works using electricity — an electric car runs on a battery'.
Abstract physics noun. Polysemous (also human energy). Drawing 'lightning bolt + battery' reads as 'electricity'. Best: 'power that makes things work or move — solar panels make energy from the sun'.
Abstract power noun. Mime 'pulling someone with strings' is too vague (could be 'control'). Best: 'the power to change what others think — TV has a big influence on kids'.
Profession defined by their output. Drawing 'person with crazy hair holding a gadget' reads as 'scientist' generically. Best: 'a person who creates new things — Marie Curie was a famous inventor'.
Abstract financial verb. Mime 'put money down then collect more' is too vague. Best: 'spend money hoping to get more back — investors put money into new companies'.
Modal adverb. Mime 'wobble hand back and forth' is too vague. Best: 'maybe — perhaps it will rain tomorrow'.
Abstract role-relation idiom. Mime 'point to chest, then to thing' is too vague. Best: 'you are the one who caused or takes care of something — I'm responsible for feeding the cat'.

Mime: hold imaginary bow/gun, aim, fire with recoil. The shooting gesture is iconic at A2 from sports and game contexts. (Note: handle gracefully in classroom — bow/arrow framing safer than firearms.)
Mime: stand tall with chest out, hands on hips, confident smile. The 'I can do this' body language reads at A2. Risk of collapse to 'brave' — actor adds a chin-up smile.
Mime: do something impressive (juggle, flex muscles), then look proudly at the audience. The 'show off' gesture reads at A2. Risk of collapse to 'show'.
Concrete object — bar of soap with bubbles, or a bottle of liquid soap. Iconic. Drawing reads instantly.
Abstract noun (any tool/gadget). Drawing one specific device collapses to that device. Best: 'a piece of equipment for a special purpose — a phone is a device'.
Abstract noun (something for sale). Drawing 'item with a price tag' is plausible but vague. Best: 'something made to sell — the shop has many new products this month'.
Abstract intensifier adjective. Mime 'jaw drop' collapses to 'amazing'. Best: 'very special, worth noticing — her achievement was remarkable'.
Mime: peer through imaginary microscope, take notes, frown thoughtfully. The lab-research gesture reads at A2. Risk of collapse to 'science'. Backup: also mime reading thick books.
Concrete body part — joint where hand meets arm, often shown with watch. Iconic. Drawing reads as 'wrist'. Show 'pointing to wrist' also works but the drawing is faster.
Concrete object — two long sticks under armpits, often with bandaged leg. Iconic at A2 from hospital/injury contexts. Drawing reads instantly.
Abstract noun (health condition). Drawing 'sick person in bed' collapses to 'sick'. Best: 'a health problem that makes you feel unwell — the flu is a common illness in winter'.
Concrete physical feature — sloped surface, often with wheelchair-accessibility icon. Iconic. Drawing reads instantly.
Concrete object — chair with two large wheels, person sitting. Iconic at A2 from accessibility contexts. Drawing reads instantly.
Abstract verb of adjustment. Mime 'change shape with hands' is too vague. Best: 'change something or yourself to fit a new situation — animals adapt to cold weather'.
Mime: hold two imaginary pieces, snap them together, click. Reads as 'connecting'. Risk of collapse to 'connect'. Backup: tape/glue motion.
Concrete clothing — five-fingered hand-shape. Iconic at A2 from winter/sports contexts. Drawing reads instantly.
Abstract compound noun (cleaning/cooking work). Drawing 'broom + dustpan + dishes' reads as 'cleaning' specifically. Best: 'work to keep a house clean — washing dishes and vacuuming are housework'.
Abstract adverb (without human action). Mime 'hands off, machine works on its own' is too vague. Best: 'works by itself — the door opens automatically when you walk close'.
Concrete clothing/pet item — band around the neck, often with tag (animal) or buttons (shirt). Iconic. Drawing reads instantly.
Abstract academic field. Drawing 'computer + circuits' is plausible but reads as 'computer'. Best: 'the school subject about how computers work and how to write programs'.
Profession. Drawing 'person with hard hat at construction' collapses to 'builder'. Best: 'a person who designs and builds machines, bridges, or roads — engineers built the new highway'.
Abstract creative-feeling noun. Mime 'lightbulb above head' is plausible but reads as 'idea'. Best: 'something that makes you want to create — my grandmother was my inspiration to become a baker'.
Mime: hammering, wrench-turning, frustrated peering at imaginary broken object then satisfied nod. Iconic at A2. (Same call as 'to fix sth.' in Unit 3 — actor varies which tool they mime.)
Abstract verb of help/backing. Mime 'pat on back + thumbs up' reads as 'good job' or 'help'. Best: 'help someone or give them what they need — my parents support me when I'm stressed'.
Mime: pretend to apply colour to hair with both hands, look in mirror, exclaim at new colour. The hair-colouring gesture is iconic at this age (peers often dye hair).
Mime: roll up sleeve, wince as imaginary needle works on arm, then admire the result. Reads at A2 from media. Risk of collapse to 'pain' or 'needle'.

rows.w: to hang out in shopping centres
rows.justification: Mime: stroll lazily with friends, browse imaginary windows, sit on a bench, look at imaginary phone. Reads as 'wandering around the mall'. Risk of collapse to 'shopping' or 'mall'.
Mime: skate motion with arms out, fall down dramatically, hold scraped knee. The two-stage gesture (skate + injury) implies 'without pads'. Risk of collapse to 'skating' alone.
Mime: point to nostril, wince as imaginary needle pierces, then admire small jewel in nose. Reads at A2 from media. Risk of collapse to 'piercing'. Backup: explain in setup.
Mime: hold imaginary phone, swipe finger up the screen repeatedly, eyes glazed. The phone-scroll gesture is universal at A2 — kids do this constantly.

rows.w: to have a party at home
rows.justification: Mime: open imaginary door for guests, dance, blow imaginary balloons up, point at imaginary house. Reads as 'party'. The 'at home' element is implicit. Risk of collapse to 'party'.

Multi-word phrase. Mime 'shopping for clothes alone, paying with own money' reads at A2 but risks collapse to 'shopping' or 'clothes'. Best: 'choose and pay for what you wear yourself, no parents helping'.
Mime: pretend to eat candy after candy, then hold stomach with sick face. The two-stage gesture (overindulge + suffer) reads at A2. Risk of collapse to 'sick' or 'eat'.
Mime: pretend to put earrings in, then point to ears with proud smile. Reads at A2. Risk of collapse to 'earrings' alone — actor adds the wearing/showing-off element.

rows.w: to ride your bike without a helmet
rows.justification: Mime: cycle motion with hands, wind in hair (touch hair with one hand while pedalling). The 'no helmet' element is shown by NOT putting one on first. Risk of collapse to 'biking'.

rows.g: nach zehn Uhr nach Hause kommen
rows.justification: Multi-word time-specific phrase. No clean mime captures '10 pm' specifically. Best: 'arrive home later than 10pm — my mum gets angry when I come home after ten'.

rows.w: to turn your music up loud
rows.justification: Mime: turn imaginary volume knob clockwise, hands to ears with grimace, head bobbing. The two-stage gesture (turn + react) reads instantly at A2.
Mime: walk to imaginary venue, then dance under flashing imaginary lights with arms in the air. Reads as 'club/disco' at A2. Risk of collapse to 'dance'.

rows.w: to play video games all day
rows.justification: Mime: hold imaginary controller, eyes glued to imaginary screen, get more tired/agitated over time. The 'gaming for hours' element shows in the slumping posture. Risk of collapse to 'video games'.
Multi-word time-specific phrase. Mime 'sit on couch watching TV' lacks the time element. Best: 'be in front of the TV later than ten — I watched TV after 10 last night'.

rows.w: to be allowed to do sth.
rows.justification: Modal-permission verb. Mime 'thumbs up + nod' is too vague. Best: 'have permission to do something — I'm allowed to stay up late on Fridays'.
Set discourse phrase. Mime 'frown with shrug' is too vague. Best: 'a way to say you're sorry about something disappointing — It's a pity you can't come to my party'.
Mime: stand tall with arms crossed, frown, point firmly with finger, mouth firm. The 'rule-enforcer' body language reads at A2 from teacher/parent contexts. Risk of collapse to 'angry'.
Polysemous (adopt a child; adopt a habit/idea). Specifically the 'start using' sense here. Mime fails to distinguish. Best: 'start using something new — many countries adopted the Euro'.
Abstract group noun. Drawing 'people standing together' reads as 'group'. Best: 'people who live in the same area or share something — our school community is friendly'.
