Abstract political/cultural adjective. Mime 'shake head at new things' is too vague. Best: 'preferring old ways, not wanting to change — my grandparents are conservative'.
Abstract compound noun. Drawing 'phone + laptop + robot' is plausible but reads as 'tech things'. Best: 'new machines and computers we use today — modern technology helps doctors save lives'.
Abstract quantifier. Mime 'arms out wide showing lots' is too vague. Best: 'more than enough, a lot — there's plenty of food at the party'.
Iconic mime — palms together, head bowed, eyes closed, mouth moving silently. Universal at A2 from many cultural contexts.

Abstract verb of consequence. Mime 'wag finger sternly + send to corner' reads at A2 from school contexts. Risk of collapse to 'angry'. Backup: explain via 'make someone suffer because they did wrong'.
Set discourse phrase. Mime 'wobble hand back and forth' is plausible but ambiguous (could be 'maybe'). Best: 'a way to say the answer changes — Will you come? It depends on the weather'.
Mime: yawn, rub eyes tiredly, look at imaginary clock with shock at how late, then keep watching TV. Reads as 'awake late'. Risk of collapse to 'tired'.
Mime: gesture 'come' to a friend, point at imaginary house, hand them an invitation card. Reads at A2. Risk of collapse to 'invite' or 'come here'.
Set idiomatic phrase. No visual or mime. Best: 'doing something different than usual — let's eat outside for a change'.

Profession. Drawing 'person with notepad and microphone' is plausible but reads as 'reporter'. Best: 'a person who writes news for a paper, TV, or website — journalists ask questions to find out what happened'.
Mime: bend down repeatedly, pick imaginary trash off ground, drop into imaginary bag. Reads as 'cleaning up trash'. Risk of collapse to 'rubbish'.
Mime: stick tongue out, make rude gesture (raspberry), interrupt loudly. The 'bad manners' body language reads at A2 from playground contexts.
Abstract intensifier adjective. Mime 'jaw drop, shake head' collapses to 'wow' or 'amazing'. Best: 'so amazing it's hard to believe — his story was unbelievable'.
Mime: shiver violently, hug self with arms crossed, teeth chatter, exaggerated cold face. Reads as 'freezing cold' at A2.
Mime: hold imaginary item, hand it to imaginary person, then point to self meaning 'give it back'. The 'temporary giving' reads at A2. Risk of collapse to 'give'. Backup: also mime 'come back to me'.
Mime: wave hand dismissively, smile, shrug. The 'forget it' gesture reads at A2. Risk of collapse to 'whatever'. Backup: actor smiles to indicate the friendly tone.
Abstract verb of memory-helping. Mime 'finger to head, then point at someone' is too vague. Best: 'help someone remember — please remind me to call mum'.

Polysemous phrasal verb (organize; resolve). Mime 'organising piles of objects into groups' reads as 'tidying'. Best: 'organise things or decide which to keep — let's sort out the books in the cupboard'.
Mime: walk with imaginary stack of papers, hand them one by one to passersby. Reads as 'distributing flyers'. The repeated action makes it specific.
Specific civic action. Mime 'sign your name on a clipboard' reads as 'sign'. Best: 'write your name on a paper to support a cause — I signed a petition to save the trees'.

rows.w: to go on a protest march
rows.justification: Mime: march in place with arms swinging, raise imaginary sign overhead, mouth chants. Reads at A2 from media. Risk of collapse to 'march' or 'walk'.
Multi-word abstract administrative phrase. Mime 'arranging chairs + writing in calendar' is too vague. Best: 'plan a get-together with people — we organised a meeting to discuss the school trip'.
Mime: type at imaginary keyboard, then click send with finger flourish, repeat for many recipients. Reads as 'sending email'. The 'out' (many) element shows in the repetition.

rows.w: to recycle paper, glass, plastic and cans
rows.g: Papier, Glas, Plastik und Dosen recyceln
rows.justification: Mime: pick up imaginary bottle, throw into different bins for each material with deliberate gestures. The 'sorting waste' reads at A2. Risk of collapse to 'throw away'.

Multi-word abstract environmental phrase. Mime 'turn off tap + turn off light' is plausible but reads as those individual actions. Best: 'use less water and electricity — switch off the tap when you brush your teeth'.
Multi-word complex phrase. Mime fails (no clear visual for 'locally'). Best: 'choose food made near you — buying locally produced apples helps farmers in your area'.
Mime: hold imaginary wrapper, start to drop it, stop yourself with stern wag of finger, then put it in a bin. The 'almost-drop then correct' two-stage action reads at A2.
Multi-word imperative phrase. Mime 'small distance with hands then no!' is too vague. Best: 'use your feet or bike for short trips — don't drive when the shop is around the corner'.

rows.w: Don't leave bottles or cans on the beach.
rows.g: Lass keine Flaschen oder Dosen am Strand liegen.
rows.justification: Multi-word imperative. Mime 'beach + bottle on sand + no!' reads as cluttered. Best: 'always take your rubbish when you leave the beach — sea animals can get hurt'.

rows.w: Don't buy a new bag. Bring your own.
rows.g: Kauf keine neue Tasche. Bring deine eigene mit.
rows.justification: Two-sentence imperative. Mime fails. Best: 'use the bags you already have — bring a cloth bag to the shop'.
Abstract noun (skill/capacity). Mime 'flex muscle + thumbs up' collapses to 'strong'. Best: 'something you can do well — she has the ability to play the piano'.
Abstract verb of being. Nothing to mime — 'being there' has no clean visual. Best: 'to be real, to be there — dragons don't exist, they're not real'.
Polysemous abstract noun (entitlement; correctness; direction). Drawing 'a list of rights' is too unspecific. Best: 'things everyone should have — kids have the right to go to school'.
Function phrase. No visual or mime. Best: 'usually, most of the time — In general, I like school'.
Abstract noun (level of goodness). Mime 'thumbs up vs thumbs down' is too binary. Best: 'how good or bad something is — this jacket is high quality, it will last for years'.
Modal-ability verb. Mime 'try and succeed' collapses to 'can'. Best: 'have the skill or chance to do something — I'm able to swim 100 metres'.
Concrete building — small house with steeply pitched roof, often in a meadow with flowers. Iconic at A2 from English picturebook contexts. Drawing reads instantly.

Abstract noun (mutual agreement). Mime 'two people meeting halfway' is plausible but vague. Best: 'an agreement where both sides give up something — we made a compromise: pizza tonight, pasta tomorrow'.

rows.g: Da ist was dran., Gutes Argument.
rows.justification: Set discourse phrase. Mime 'finger up + thoughtful nod' is too vague. Best: 'a way to say someone has a strong argument — Good point, I hadn't thought of that'.
Idiomatic verb (act, not just talk). Mime 'roll up sleeves + step forward' is plausible but vague. Best: 'do something about a problem — let's take action and clean up the park'.
Iconic building — large old building with clock tower or columns, often with a flag. Recognizable from many European towns. Drawing reads instantly.
Polysemous (literal exit; figurative solution). Drawing 'EXIT sign' captures the literal sense. Best: 'a solution to a difficult problem — there's no easy way out of this situation'.
Abstract math/social noun. Mime 'point to a big group + small group' is too vague. Best: 'more than half — the majority of students like sports'.

Polysemous (reasoned point; quarrel). Mime 'two people shouting at each other' captures the quarrel sense but misses the reasoned-point sense. Best: 'a reason for or against, or a fight with words — they had an argument about money'.
Mime: march in place with imaginary sign held up, mouth chants, frown. Reads at A2 from news contexts. Risk of overlap with 'protest march' — actor uses just sign + chant, no marching motion.
Abstract local-government body. Drawing 'group at a table' is too generic. Best: 'the group of people who make decisions for a town — the city council voted to build a new park'.
Concrete object — fabric tote bag with handles, sometimes with a slogan. Iconic at A2 from environmental contexts. Drawing reads instantly.
Function adverb of frequency. Mime 'shake head + raise tiny fingers' is too vague. Best: 'almost never — I hardly ever eat fast food'.
Mime: lounge on imaginary sofa, yawn, refuse to get up, swat away imaginary chores. The 'I won't move' body language reads at A2 instantly.
Concrete physical material — paper or plastic around a present or product. Drawing 'wrapped present with bow' or 'plastic bag around food' reads. Risk of collapse to 'present' specifically.
Mime: stand up tall, point at someone behind you, defend with arms out. The 'protect/defend' gesture reads at A2. Risk of collapse to 'defend'. Backup: explain via 'speaking up for what's right'.
Abstract historical/political noun. No visual or mime. Best: 'the right to vote — suffrage for women came in 1918 in Austria'.

Specific historical role. Drawing 'woman with sash and banner' reads at A2 from textbook. Best in words to capture historical context: 'a woman who fought for the right to vote — Emmeline Pankhurst was a famous suffragette'.
Mime: pick up imaginary ballot, mark X with imaginary pen, fold and place in imaginary box. The voting ritual reads at A2 from civic-education contexts.
Abstract verb of going to an event/school. Mime 'walking into a building, taking a seat' is too generic. Best: 'go to an event, school, or meeting — only ten people attended the meeting'.
Abstract relational verb. Mime 'point at two things side by side, equals sign' is too vague. Best: 'have the same rights and be treated the same — boys and girls should be equal'.
Abstract noun (governmental rule). Drawing 'gavel + book' reads as 'judge/courtroom'. Best: 'a rule made by the government — there's a law against speeding'.
Time adverb. No visual referent. Mime 'point to ground/now' is too vague. Best: 'these days, in the present time — Nowadays, everyone has a phone'.

Polysemous abstract verb (handle a person; medical treatment; provide a treat). Mime 'pat someone gently + give present' collapses. Best: 'act towards someone in a certain way — please treat your sister kindly'.

Mime: pretend to be police, grab imaginary suspect's arm, put on imaginary handcuffs, march them away. The arresting sequence reads at A2 from media. Note: definition gloss says it's a noun ('arrest') but the verb sense is what's mimable.
Abstract noun (formal learning). Drawing 'school + university + books' reads as 'school'. Best: 'learning at school or university — education is important for getting a good job'.

rows.g: sich für etw./jdn. aussprechen, seine Meinung sagen
rows.justification: Mime: stand at imaginary microphone, point firmly, mouth strong words. Reads as 'public speaking'. Risk of collapse to 'speech' or 'talk'.
Mime: cross arms in big X, shake head firmly, take a step back from offered imaginary item. The 'firm no' body language reads at A2.
Mime: pull down imaginary shop shutter, lock with imaginary key, hang up 'CLOSED' sign. The shop-closure gesture reads at A2. Risk of collapse to 'close'.
Abstract negative-compound adjective. Mime 'fists then no, hands open' is too vague. Best: 'without using force or hurting people — Gandhi believed in non-violent protest'.
Iconic visual — figure in suit and tie carrying a briefcase. Drawing reads at A2. Risk of overlap with 'suit' from Unit 1 — actor adds the briefcase.
Abstract noun (worry/issue). Mime 'furrowed brow + hand to chin' collapses to 'worried'. Best: 'something that worries you or is important — my main concern is the climate'.

Abstract noun (formal discussion). Mime 'two people with podiums arguing' is plausible but specific. Best: 'a formal discussion where people share different opinions — there was a debate about the new rules'.
Specific profession. Drawing 'person at school office desk' is generic. Best: 'the person in charge of a school — Mrs Wagner is our headteacher'.
Abstract verb of inclusion. Mime 'wave someone in to a circle' is too vague. Best: 'include someone in an activity or decision — we should involve the parents in this discussion'.
Abstract group noun. Drawing 'logo on sign' is too unspecific. Best: 'a group of people working together for a purpose — Greenpeace is an organisation that helps the environment'.
Iconic geological feature — deep V-shaped valley with steep walls and a small river at the bottom. The Grand Canyon is a known reference. Drawing reads instantly.
Concrete physical feature — winding dusty path through countryside, no asphalt. Drawing reads as 'unpaved road'. Risk of collapse to 'road' — actor adds dust clouds and rough surface.
Concrete geological feature — long narrow mountaintop with steep sides. Drawing reads as 'mountain top' or 'ridge'. Risk of collapse to 'mountain' — actor draws a clear ridgeline silhouette.
Abstract organizational noun. Drawing 'big office building' is too generic. Best: 'the main office of a company — Apple's headquarters is in California'.

Mime: scan the horizon, suddenly point with finger and exaggerated 'aha!' face. Reads as 'see/notice'. Risk of collapse to 'see' or 'find'. Backup: actor adds 'difficult to see' element by squinting first.

Multi-word concrete-but-vague phrase. Drawing 'cracked desert ground with sun' captures the dryness. Best in words to specify any dry place: 'a place with very little rain — the desert is a dry place'.
Mime: hold imaginary phone up high, look at screen frowning, shake phone, walk to different spots. Reads as 'phone problem'. Risk of collapse to 'no internet'.
Concrete object — bag with two straps over shoulders, often with pockets. Iconic at A2. Drawing reads instantly.
Abstract intensifier adjective. Mime 'jaw drop + thumbs up' collapses to 'great'. Best: 'wonderful, extremely good — that was a fabulous concert!'
Abstract measurement noun. Drawing 'tall thing with arrow up' reads as 'tall'. Best: 'how tall something is, from bottom to top — what's the height of the tower?'

Polysemous abstract noun (capital city; capital letter; capital money). Drawing 'star on map' is plausible. Best in words to specify the city sense: 'the most important city of a country — Vienna is the capital of Austria'.
Abstract adjective (free of control). Mime 'cut imaginary string + walk away alone' is plausible but vague. Best: 'free and not controlled by others — Austria became independent in 1918'.
Abstract noun (new idea/method). Drawing 'lightbulb + gadget' reads as 'invention/idea'. Best: 'a new idea or method — using AI in schools is a new innovation'.

Polysemous (country; condition; US state). Drawing 'flag + borders' is too vague. Best in words to specify the political-unit sense: 'a country, or part of a country with its own government — Texas is a state in the USA'.
Mime: get on imaginary train with briefcase, sit down looking tired, then get off and walk to office. The 'home-to-work travel' two-stage gesture reads at A2. Risk of collapse to 'travel'.

Polysemous abstract noun (link; relationship; transport link; internet). Drawing 'two dots with line between' is too generic. Best: 'a link between two things — there's a good connection between the two cities'.
Profession defined by activity. Drawing 'person at laptop with code on screen' reads as 'computer person'. Best: 'a person who writes code for computers — programmers make apps and websites'.
Concrete physical descriptor — sharp angle of a slope. Drawing 'a hill at very sharp angle' reads. Mime 'climbing up steeply with effort' is also possible. Drawing wins on clarity of the angle.

Polysemous (break with a sound; crack a code; crack a joke). Mime 'snap two hands together as if breaking something' captures the physical sense. Risk: collapses to 'break'. Backup: explain the 'with a sharp sound' nuance.
Compound technical noun. Drawing 'rugged off-road vehicle (Jeep) on rough terrain' reads at A2 from media. Risk of collapse to 'car' or 'jeep'. Best with explicit 4×4 sticker drawn on the side.

Iconic visual — figure with pickaxe and pan kneeling by river, gold flecks visible. Draws on shared cartoon imagery from Western/Disney. Risk of collapse to 'miner'. Backup: actor includes specific gold-pan.
Specific historical event/period. Drawing fails (too narrative). Best: 'a time when many people hurried to find gold — there was a gold rush in California in 1848'.
Concrete body part — close-up of mouth showing upper and lower lips. Iconic. Drawing reads instantly. Show 'pointing at lips' is also fine but the close-up sketch is unambiguous.
Concrete geological feature — series of triangular peaks connected, forming a horizon line. Drawing reads instantly at A2.

Abstract concept (area without sun). Drawing 'tree with figure underneath in dark area' reads. Best in words to specify cleanly: 'an area not in direct sunlight — let's sit in the shade, it's cooler there'.
Formal abstract verb of location. Mime 'point at imaginary map' is too vague. Best: 'be in a place — Vienna is situated on the Danube'.
Mime: hold throat with tongue out, fan self desperately, mime drinking from imaginary jug greedily. Reads as 'thirsty/thirst' at A2 (related to the adjective from Unit 3 'thirsty').
Person noun defined by behaviour. Mime 'sneaky person stealing' reads as 'thief' specifically. Best: 'a person who breaks the law — the police are looking for the criminal'.
Iconic visual — figure on bicycle, often in helmet and lycra. Drawing reads instantly at A2. Show 'pretending to bike' captures the verb 'to cycle'.
Abstract adjective. Mime 'pointing at imaginary thing with knowing nod' is too vague. Best: 'well known to you — the route to school is familiar, I take it every day'.
Concrete vehicle — large flat boat carrying cars and people. Iconic. Drawing reads as 'ferry' at A2.
Abstract adjective (led by someone). Mime 'someone leading a group' reads as 'tour' specifically. Best: 'led by someone who shows you around — we took a guided tour of the museum'.
Abstract phrasal verb (assume control). Mime 'one person stepping into another's place at a desk' reads at A2 but vague. Best: 'get control of something — the new manager took over the company'.
Mime: run with bag toward imaginary train, jump on at last moment with relief. The 'just-make-it' gesture reads at A2. Risk of collapse to 'run'.
Concrete location — small booth or counter with 'i' or '?' sign, brochures visible. Drawing reads as 'info point'. Risk of collapse to 'shop' — actor adds the 'i' symbol.
Concrete infrastructure — train tracks with sleepers, sometimes with a train on them. Iconic. Drawing reads instantly.
Adverb of degree. Mime 'arms wide showing 100%' is too vague. Best: 'completely, 100% — I totally agree with you'.
Concrete environmental scene — cracked dry earth, dead plants, sun beating down. Iconic at A2 from news/textbook. Drawing reads as 'no water/dry'.
Mime: shake whole body, stagger from side to side, things falling around you. The full-body trembling reads as 'earthquake' at A2 from media.

Iconic visual — spiral of clouds with arrow showing wind direction, often with palm trees bending. Drawing reads at A2 from weather contexts. Show 'wind blowing arms around' is also possible. Drawing wins on the spiral specificity.
Iconic visual — cone-shaped mountain with red/orange lava and ash erupting from top. Universally recognizable at A2. Drawing reads instantly.
Concrete disaster scene — brown earth flowing down a hill, sometimes burying houses. Drawing reads as 'mud falling'. Risk of collapse to 'mud' — actor adds motion arrows.
Concrete winter disaster — large white wave of snow rolling down a mountain, sometimes burying skiers. Drawing reads at A2 from Alpine contexts.
Iconic disaster — trees with red/orange flames, smoke rising. Drawing reads instantly at A2 from news contexts.
Iconic visual — huge wave with curl, often with small boats in front for scale. Universally recognizable at A2. Drawing reads instantly.
Concrete scene — houses or streets underwater, sometimes with people wading. Iconic at A2 from news contexts. Drawing reads as 'flooded'.

Multi-word abstract phrase (practice exercise). Mime 'leaving building in line' captures evacuation but not the 'practice' element. Best: 'practice exercise for fire emergency — we have a fire drill at school every term'.
Concrete sign-style image — building floor plan with arrow pointing to exit. Drawing reads at A2 from school posters. Show 'pretending to follow path to exit' is also possible. Drawing is faster.
Concrete object — round white disc on ceiling, often with light. Drawing reads at A2 from home/school contexts. Risk of collapse to 'alarm'. Backup: actor adds smoke wisps below.
Multi-word concrete-but-vague noun. Drawing 'X marks the spot' is too generic. Best: 'where everyone gathers after an emergency — our meeting place is the playground'.
Mime: walk to imaginary door, place hand on it carefully (testing for heat), then open or move to next door. Reads at A2 from fire-safety lessons. Risk of collapse to 'opening doors'.
Mime: drop to hands and knees, move along the floor staying very low, arm over face. The fire-safety crawl-under-smoke is iconic at A2 from fire drills.
Iconic three-stage fire-safety mime — freeze, drop to ground, roll body side to side. Universal at A2 from fire-safety lessons. Pure show.
Abstract noun (careful study). Mime 'reading + writing notes' reads as 'study'. Best: 'careful study to find new facts — scientists do research on the climate'.
Mime: pretend to be in a tight space, push against imaginary walls, panicked face, bang on imaginary door. Reads as 'stuck'. Risk of collapse to 'scared' or 'closed'.

Polysemous abstract noun (physical force; mental stress). Mime 'press hands together hard' captures the physical sense. Best in words to handle both senses: 'when something pushes against something — the pressure underwater is very high'.
Abstract noun (top/outside of something). Drawing 'flat plane with arrow' is too vague. Best: 'the outside or top part of something — the surface of the lake was calm'.
Compound concrete adjective — fish, seaweed, coral, all below a wavy water line. Drawing reads at A2. Risk of collapse to 'sea'. Backup: actor adds bubbles/divers.
Concrete geographic feature — line on map or fence on ground separating two flagged territories. Drawing reads as 'border' at A2 from geography contexts.
Abstract noun (harm done to something). Drawing 'broken object' is too specific (which thing?). Best: 'harm done to something — the storm caused a lot of damage to the houses'.
Mime: line of people walking quickly out of building, look back at danger, follow arrow signs. Reads as 'leaving in emergency'. Risk of collapse to 'leave'. Backup: emergency-exit framing.
Mime: hold imaginary ruler against object, point and read carefully, write down number. The measuring gesture is iconic at A2 from school maths/PE contexts.
Abstract geographic noun. Drawing 'circle on map' is too vague. Best: 'a large area of land — the Alps are a mountain region'.
Mime: angry face, fists raised, threatening lunge (without making contact). The aggression body language reads at A2. Risk of collapse to 'angry' — actor exaggerates physical intent.
Mime: walk toward imaginary danger sign, recoil with hands up, take big step back. The 'don't go near!' gesture reads at A2. Risk of collapse to 'no'.
Mime: trip, stumble, fall to the ground (controlled), look up surprised. Reads as 'falling' instantly at A2.
Abstract verb of sudden understanding. Mime 'aha! lightbulb gesture' reads at A2 from cartoon contexts. Risk of collapse to 'understand' or 'idea'. Backup: explain via 'suddenly understand'.
Abstract noun (staying alive). Drawing 'figure on island with sun and basic shelter' is plausible but specific. Best: 'staying alive in danger — survival in the wild needs water, food, and shelter'.
Preposition. Mime 'duck under imaginary table' is plausible but reads as 'under'. Best: 'below or under — the cat is underneath the table'.

Concrete substance — grey powder, often shown after fire or with cigarette/volcano. Drawing 'pile of grey dust' reads. Risk of collapse to 'dust' or 'sand'. Backup: actor draws a wisp of smoke nearby.
Iconic visual — figure alone on small island with palm tree, often waving for help at boat. Drawing reads at A2 from Robinson Crusoe references. Universal.
Mime: carry imaginary parcel, knock on imaginary door, hand it over with smile, get signature. The delivery gesture is iconic at A2 from Amazon/post contexts.
Compound abstract noun. Drawing 'truck with logo + parcels' is plausible but slow. Best: 'a business that brings things to people's homes — DHL is a delivery company'.
Concrete physical feature — pointed orange/yellow shape with red base. Iconic and quick to sketch. Drawing reads instantly at A2.
Idiomatic verb of habituation. Mime 'first uncomfortable then okay' is too vague. Best: 'become comfortable with something — I got used to the early mornings at the new school'.
Compound abstract noun (where you grew up). Drawing 'familiar town with heart' is plausible but vague. Best: 'the town where you grew up — my hometown is Vienna, I miss it when I travel'.
Mime: huge smile, jump up and down with arms in the air, hug self. The pure-happy body language reads at A2. Risk of overlap with 'happy' — actor exaggerates the leap and shout.
Concrete object — rectangular box with paper/string and label, sometimes with stamps. Iconic. Drawing reads instantly at A2.
Concrete object — flat platform of logs tied together, floating on water. Iconic at A2 from adventure stories. Drawing reads instantly.

Concrete safe space — simple structure (lean-to, tarp tent, small hut) often with figure inside. Drawing reads as 'shelter/safe place'. Risk of collapse to 'house' — actor draws something more rough/temporary.
Abstract verb of transformation. Mime 'something becomes something' is too vague. Best: 'become something different — water turns into ice when it freezes'.
Abstract noun (amazing, unexplainable thing). Mime 'jaw drop, hands up, look at sky' collapses to 'wow'. Best: 'something amazing you can't explain — it's a miracle the cat survived'.
Iconic visual — small round island with one palm tree, surrounded by water. Universal at A2 from cartoons. Drawing reads instantly.
Abstract feeling noun. Mime 'contented sigh + smile' collapses to 'happy'. Best: 'a feeling of enjoyment — reading is a pleasure for me'.
Function phrase. No visual or mime. Best: 'if something happens — In case of fire, leave the building'.
Concrete object — small rectangular device with flame at top. Iconic at A2. Drawing reads instantly. Show 'thumb-flick gesture' is plausible but slower.
Mime: stand up tall, then suddenly buckle at the knees and fall to the ground in slow motion. Reads as 'falling apart/collapsing'. Risk of overlap with 'fall down' — actor adds the gradual buckling.
Idiomatic decision-making phrase. Closely related to 'make up one's mind' from Unit 7 — same handling. Best: 'decide after thinking — I made up my mind to study harder'.
Idiomatic phrase about delayed decisions. Mime 'pillow under head + tomorrow gesture' is too vague. Best: 'wait until tomorrow to decide — I'll sleep on it and tell you in the morning'.

rows.w: to find a way out of a dilemma
rows.g: einen Ausweg aus einem Dilemma finden
rows.justification: Multi-word abstract phrase. Mime fails. Best: 'find a solution to a difficult problem — it took us a week to find a way out of the dilemma'.

rows.w: to be in two minds about sth.
rows.justification: Idiomatic phrase about indecision. Mime 'looking left then right with uncertain face' is plausible but vague. Best: 'unsure because you think both yes and no — I'm in two minds about going to the party'.

rows.w: to have second thoughts about sth.
rows.justification: Idiomatic phrase (reconsider). Mime 'finger to chin then frown' collapses to 'thinking'. Best: 'start thinking maybe your first idea wasn't good — I had second thoughts about my haircut'.
Idiom about confusion. Mime 'shrug + confused face' collapses to 'don't know'. Best: 'not knowing what to do or say — I was at a loss when she started crying'.
Abstract noun (difficult choice). Mime 'two paths with hands' is too vague. Best: 'a difficult situation where you must choose between two things — I have a dilemma: party or homework?'
Idiomatic phrase. Mime 'finger up with confident nod' collapses to 'decide'. Best: 'finally decide after thinking — we reached a decision after a long meeting'.
Mime: hold imaginary phone, mouth 'sorry, I can't', or wave hands in big X over an imaginary calendar. Reads as 'calling off'. Risk of collapse to 'no'. Backup: actor adds the calendar-X gesture.
Mime: open imaginary present with eager face, then deflate with sad face and shoulders down. The two-stage gesture (hope → fall) reads at A2. Risk of collapse to 'sad'.
Iconic visual — older man with grey hair, possibly glasses, smile lines. Drawing reads at A2 from family contexts. Show 'imitating an old man with cane' is also possible but reads more as 'old'.
Mime: point sternly at imaginary person, jerk thumb over shoulder ('out!'), shake head no. Reads as 'remove from group'. Risk of collapse to 'go away'.

Polysemous (move physically; move house; reschedule). Specifically the 'reschedule' sense here. Mime 'moving date on calendar' is too specific. Best: 'change the time of something — they moved the meeting to Thursday'.
Abstract verb. Mime 'wave hand to pause + think again' is too vague. Best: 'think about something again — I rethought my plan after talking to mum'.
Abstract verb (have earned). Mime 'crown on head + thumbs up' collapses to 'good job'. Best: 'have earned something good or bad — she deserves a prize for her hard work'.
Function preposition. Mime 'point to group, then exclude one with X' is plausible but vague. Best: 'not including — Everyone came except Tom'.
Set discourse phrase. Mime 'frown + headshake' collapses to 'sad'. Best: 'a way to say you feel sorry about something — It's a shame you can't come'.

Polysemous (elevator; rise up; ride). Specifically the 'free ride' sense here. Mime 'thumbs out hitchhiking + getting in car' is plausible but reads as 'hitchhike'. Best: 'a free ride in someone's car — can you give me a lift to school?'
Specific abstract noun (proof of being elsewhere). No clean mime. Best: 'proof that you were somewhere else when something bad happened — the suspect had an alibi'.
Concrete object — card with photo, name, and birthdate. Iconic at A2. Drawing reads as 'ID card' instantly.
Iconic mime — finger to lips ('shhh!'), look around conspiratorially. Universal at A2.
Mime: cup hand to mouth, lean in to whisper to imaginary teacher while pointing at someone. Reads as 'snitching' at A2. Risk of collapse to 'whisper'.

Specific school-context noun. Drawing 'student alone at desk after school' is plausible but reads as 'studying'. Best: 'a punishment to stay at school after classes — Tom got detention for being late'.
Mime: hold imaginary poster, reach up to wall, press into place with both hands. Reads as 'hanging on wall' at A2. Universal.
Idiomatic phrasal verb (ask on a date). Mime 'shy boy with flowers approaches girl' reads at A2 from media but potentially awkward. Best: 'invite someone on a date — he asked her out to the cinema'.
Mime: pretend to bump into something, then look surprised with hands up ('I didn't mean it!'). Reads as 'by mistake' at A2. Risk of collapse to 'oops'.

Mime: face imaginary person, gesticulate angrily, mouth strong words, point fingers. The 'two people fighting verbally' reads at A2. Risk of overlap with 'argument' — actor emphasises the verb action.
Mime: see imaginary problem, then deliberately turn head and walk away whistling. Reads as 'pretending not to notice' at A2. Universal.
Mime: act sick with thermometer, then secretly grin to camera (or audience). The 'fake act with knowing wink' reads at A2 from cartoon contexts. Risk of collapse to whatever's being faked.
Mime: imaginary person offers something, recipient pushes it away with firm head-shake. Reads as 'refuse' or 'reject'. Risk of overlap with 'to refuse' from Unit 10.
Compound adjective. Drawing 'jar of jam with hand-written label' is plausible but specific. Best: 'made at home, not bought — homemade cookies are the best'.
Function phrase. Mime 'point to two things, X both' is too vague. Best: 'not one and not the other — neither of my brothers came to the party'.
Concrete object — paper with monetary value, often with €/$ symbol and barcode. Drawing reads as 'gift voucher' at A2. Risk of collapse to 'money' or 'ticket'.
Mime: place imaginary item on paper, fold corners up, tie a bow on top with flourish. The gift-wrapping gesture is iconic at A2 from birthday/Christmas contexts.

Multi-word abstract verb. Mime 'looking at map and writing in calendar' is plausible but reads as 'planning' generically. Best: 'organise a holiday or journey — let's plan a trip to Italy this summer'.
Mime: type at imaginary computer, click 'book now' button, smile, take a screenshot. Reads as 'online booking'. Risk of collapse to 'computer' — actor adds the satisfied 'done!' moment.
Mime: hold imaginary phone, mouth dates and 'two rooms please', write in imaginary calendar. Reads as 'phone booking'. Risk of overlap with 'to make a reservation' from Unit 3.
Multi-word abstract verb. Mime 'sign paper + receive keys' is plausible but reads as 'rent'. Best: 'pay to use a car for a short time — we hired a car for our holiday'.

rows.w: to check the area out online
rows.justification: Mime: type/scroll on imaginary laptop, point at imaginary map on screen, nod. Reads as 'researching online'. Risk of collapse to 'computer'.
Mime: at imaginary bookshop, pick up thick book, flip through alphabetical pages, hand over money. Reads at A2. Risk of collapse to 'buy book' — actor mimes flipping through letters.

rows.w: to find out about good restaurants
rows.justification: Multi-word abstract phrase. Mime fails (no clean visual for 'good restaurants'). Best: 'search for nice places to eat — I found out about a great pizza place online'.

rows.w: to find information about the best beaches
rows.g: Informationen über die besten Strände finden
rows.justification: Multi-word complex phrase. Mime fails. Best: 'search for details on the nicest beaches — I'm finding information about the best beaches in Greece'.

rows.w: to look at a map of the area
rows.g: sich eine Karte der Gegend ansehen
rows.justification: Mime: open imaginary map (large gesture with both arms wide), point and trace routes with finger, nod thoughtfully. Reads at A2 as 'studying a map'. Risk of collapse to 'map'.

rows.w: to find out what to do there
rows.g: herausfinden, was man dort machen kann
rows.justification: Multi-word complex phrase. Mime fails. Best: 'learn about things to do at a place — I want to find out what to do in Vienna'.
Concrete small creature — round body, six legs, often with antennae. Drawing reads as 'insect'. Risk of overlap with 'beetle/spider/fly'. Backup: actor adds simple buzzing motion lines.
Abstract verb (like one more than another). Mime 'thumb up at A vs thumb down at B' is plausible but vague. Best: 'like one thing more than another — I prefer tea to coffee'.
Compound abstract noun. Drawing 'flag + speech bubble' is too vague. Best: 'the main language used by a country's government — German is the official language of Austria'.
Concrete architectural feature — small platform sticking out of a building wall, with a railing. Iconic at A2. Drawing reads instantly.
Abstract noun (illegal act). Drawing 'masked thief' or 'police tape' collapses to specific crimes. Best: 'something against the law — stealing is a crime'.
Mime: hold imaginary shovel, push it into ground with foot, lift, throw dirt over shoulder. The digging gesture is iconic at A2 from gardening/treasure-hunting contexts.
Mime: hands fly to face, jaw drops wide, eyes huge, take a step back. The shock-reaction body language is iconic at A2 from cartoon contexts.
Compound concrete noun. Drawing 'lion or wolf in wild setting (no cage, no leash)' reads as 'wild creature'. Risk of collapse to specific animal — actor draws a generic profile of a fierce beast.
Concrete environmental feature — marshy area with reeds, water, possibly a frog or bird. Drawing reads at A2 from geography contexts. Risk of collapse to 'swamp' or 'pond'.
Function adverb. Mime 'point to A then turn to B with warning face' is too vague. Best: 'if not, or else — Hurry up, otherwise we'll be late'.

Polysemous adjective (filled with material; very full from eating). Drawing 'taxidermy bear in museum pose' captures the specific sense here. Best in words to clarify: 'filled with material to keep its shape — like a stuffed teddy bear or a stuffed animal in a museum'.
Compound abstract noun (wild animals + plants). Drawing 'forest scene with various animals visible' reads as 'nature/wildlife'. Risk of collapse to 'forest' or 'animals'.
Adverb of immediacy. Mime 'snap fingers + go!' is too vague. Best: 'right now, immediately — Come here at once!'
Concrete tree part — line growing out from a thicker trunk, often with leaves. Iconic. Drawing reads instantly at A2.
Discourse marker. No visual or mime. Best: 'used to add something to a conversation — By the way, did you see the news?'
Mime: rude actions — interrupt, push past, take without asking. The bad-manners cluster reads at A2. Risk of overlap with 'rude' from Unit 9 — actor uses different specific actions.

rows.g: um eine Ecke, um eine Kurve
rows.justification: Concrete physical configuration — winding road with arrow showing curve. Drawing reads as 'around a curve'. Risk of collapse to 'corner'. Backup: car going round the bend.
Concrete plant — short rounded green shape, often with small flowers/berries. Iconic at A2. Drawing reads instantly.
Concrete physical injury — line with red drops on skin (arm or finger). Drawing reads as 'cut/wound'. Risk of overlap with 'rash' or 'injury' — actor adds the linear shape vs spots.
Mime: get into imaginary car, slam door, grip wheel, accelerate fast away with engine sound (mouthed). The 'leaving in a car' reads at A2. Risk of overlap with 'to drive'.
Concrete object — block with cylinders, pistons, sometimes wires; often shown under car bonnet. Drawing reads at A2 from car contexts. Risk of collapse to 'machine'.
Concrete part — car interior with two seats highlighted at the front, near the steering wheel. Drawing reads. Risk of collapse to 'seat' — actor adds the steering wheel for context.

Specific profession. Drawing 'figure in uniform with hat in nature park' is plausible but specific. Best: 'a person who works in a nature park and looks after it — the park ranger told us not to feed the deer'.
Concrete physical condition — bright red skin, often with peeling, contrast with white where shorts/shirt covered. Drawing reads at A2 from summer contexts. Risk of collapse to 'red' or 'pain'.
Mime: rotate body upside down (or with hands showing a flipping motion). Reads as 'flipping over'. Universal at A2 from gymnastics/car-crash contexts.
Iconic mime — hand cupped beside mouth, lean toward listener, mouth words very small. Universal at A2.
Mime: clap hands hard together, then both arms fly up + shocked face. The collision-then-shock two-stage gesture reads at A2. Risk of collapse to 'accident'.

rows.g: eine Organisation, die sich für fairen Handel einsetzt
an die Tür gehen, jdn hereinlassen
ab und zu; hin und wieder

rows.justification: Abstract mental state. Mime 'finger to head + raised eyebrow' is too vague (could be 'think' or 'know'). Best: 'know that something is happening — be aware of cars when you cross the road'.
Religious affiliation/identity. Drawing 'cross + church' reads as 'church/Christian' generically. Best: 'belonging to the Catholic Church, led by the Pope — most people in Ireland are Catholic'.
Abstract adjective about language ability. Mime 'speaking fast with confidence' collapses to 'speak'. Best: 'able to speak a language smoothly — she's fluent in three languages'.
Abstract adjective. Same call as G3's 'independent' — drawing 'cut string + walk away' is too vague. Best: 'free, not controlled by others — Ireland became independent from the UK'.
Abstract adjective. Mime 'pointing forward with confidence' collapses to 'lead' or 'first'. Best: 'most important or most successful — she's a leading scientist'.
Abstract role. Same as G3: drawing 'figure stepping into circle' is vague. Best: 'a person who belongs to a group — I'm a member of the football team'.

Concrete location — small school building with smaller children at desks or in playground. Drawing reads at A2+ from school contexts. Risk of collapse to 'school' generally — actor adds the smaller-kid element.
Concrete farm animals — cows in a field, often more than one. Iconic at A2+ from rural visuals. Drawing reads instantly.
Iconic mime — arms up, fist-pumping, big smile, mouth 'yay!' as if celebrating sport win. Universal at A2+ from match contexts.
Concrete — rows of wheat or vegetables in a farm field. Iconic at A2+. Drawing reads as 'harvest/crops'.
Abstract historical concept (mass hunger). Drawing 'thin people in field' is potentially upsetting. Best: 'when many people have no food — the Irish potato famine'.

Polysemous (also past of 'to find'). Specifically the 'establish' sense. Mime 'planting a flag and naming a place' is plausible but vague. Best: 'start an organisation or city — Rome was founded long ago'.
Abstract political concept. Drawing 'flag + crown crossed out' is too specific. Best: 'a country that governs itself — the Irish Free State was created in 1922'.
Concrete biological object — mushroom or mould. Iconic mushroom silhouette at A2+. Drawing reads instantly.
Abstract institution. Same as G3. Best: 'the people who run a country — the government makes the laws'.
Concrete substance — wheat stalks with grain heads, or rice/barley grains. Iconic at A2+. Drawing reads as 'cereal/wheat'.

Abstract noun (event, often unpleasant). Mime 'something happened with shocked face' collapses to 'shock/event'. Best: 'an event, often unusual or unpleasant — there was a strange incident at school today'.
Abstract noun (plan/aim). Mime 'finger to chin then point forward' collapses to 'plan'. Best: 'a plan to do something — my intention is to study harder this year'.
Mime: lean into an imaginary conversation, butt in with hands waving, get pushed away. Reads as 'getting involved where not wanted'. Risk of collapse to 'talk' or 'push'.
Person defined by ownership relation. Drawing 'figure with house + key' reads as 'owner'. Best: 'a person who owns a house and rents it to others — my landlord wants more rent next year'.
Abstract math/social noun. Same as G3. Best: 'more than half — the majority of students like sports'.
Polysemous phrasal verb (literal place down; quell rebellion; criticise). Specifically 'quell' here. Mime fails to disambiguate. Best: 'stop a protest by force — the army put down the rebellion'.
Iconic mime — extend right hand, grip imaginary partner's hand, shake firmly with smile. Universal at A2+.
Mime: clutch stomach with weakened body, fall to knees, beg for food with open mouth. Visceral and unmistakable at A2+.
Set imperative. Mime 'finger up + question face' is too vague. Best: 'a way to tell someone to try to find the answer — Guess what colour I'm thinking of!'
Modal preference phrase. Mime 'point at A then B with preference face' is too vague. Best: 'used to say what you prefer — I'd rather have pizza than salad'.
Identity noun. Drawing 'figure with passport + suitcase' reads as 'tourist/traveller'. Best: 'a person from a different country — there are many foreigners visiting Vienna in summer'.
Abstract verb. Same as G3. Best: 'make something better — I want to improve my English'.
Abstract financial noun. Drawing 'money + government building' is vague. Best: 'money that people pay to the government — we pay tax on what we buy'.
Mime: walk in place with backpack on shoulders, walking-stick gesture, look around at nature, breathe deep. Reads at A2+ from many shared outdoor contexts.
Abstract qualifier adjective. Mime 'thumbs up with serious face' collapses to 'good'. Best: 'correct, suitable — wear proper shoes for hiking, not flip-flops'.
Mime: look at imaginary object (statue, painting) with hand on chest, head tilt, awed sigh. Reads at A2+ from museum contexts. Risk of collapse to 'look'.
Mime: hands to face, scream silently, shake violently, eyes wide, take steps back. Visceral at A2+. The exaggerated terror reads more than 'scared' alone.
Abstract noun + discourse marker. Mime 'wave hand dismissively' collapses to 'no' or 'whatever'. Best: 'silly words with no meaning — that's nonsense, dragons aren't real'.

Iconic visual — lightning bolt with dark cloud. Drawing reads as 'storm/thunder' instantly at A2+ (note: drawing represents the noun 'thunder' even though it's technically about sound — visual shorthand at this age uses lightning to mean both).
Mime: stand normally, then suddenly faint to the ground in a heap, lie still with eyes closed. The full collapse reads at A2+ from medical/sports contexts.
Abstract legal status. Drawing 'red NO sign over an action' is too vague (which action?). Best: 'not allowed by the law — it's illegal to drive without a licence'.

Abstract role-noun (person believed to have done it). Drawing 'figure with question mark above head' is plausible but vague. Best: 'a person the police think might have done a crime — there are three suspects in the case'.
Same call as G3 — drawing 'sneaky figure stealing' reads as 'thief'. Best: 'a person who breaks the law — the police caught the criminal'.
Iconic mime — sneaky walk, look around, grab quickly, hide. Universal at A2+ from cartoon/film conventions.
Abstract noun (proof). Drawing 'magnifying glass + papers + footprint' reads as 'detective stuff'. Best: 'facts that show something is true — the police have evidence that he did it'.
Same as G3. Best: 'a person hurt or harmed — there were three victims of the crash'.
Same as G3. Best: 'forcing someone to do what you want by threatening to tell their secret'.
Specific abstract crime. Mime is potentially upsetting in classroom. Best: 'killing another person on purpose — murder is the worst crime'.
Concrete object category. Drawing 'sword + hammer + bow' (non-firearm options safer for classroom) reads as 'weapons'. Risk of collapse to 'sword'/'gun'. Backup: warning-sign frame around the weapon.

Abstract role-noun (person who saw it). Mime 'figure with hand on Bible swearing' is plausible but specific to courtroom. Best: 'a person who saw a crime happen — the witness told the police what she saw'.
Concrete body part — outline of torso pointing to chest area. Iconic at A2+. Drawing reads instantly. Show 'pointing to own chest' also works but the sketch disambiguates from heart/stomach.
Abstract role-noun. Drawing 'figure at desk with badge' reads as generic 'worker'. Best: 'a person paid to work for a company — there are 200 employees at this office'.
Abstract noun. Mime 'shrug + question mark gesture' collapses to 'what?'. Best: 'something strange that hasn't been explained — the missing keys are a mystery'.
Same as G3 — drawing 'paper with text' reads as 'document'. Best: 'a written account of what happened — the police wrote a report about the crime'.
Mime: look at imaginary person with admiring eyes, hand on chest, raised eyebrow. Reads as 'good-looking'. Risk of collapse to 'beautiful' — actor uses the focused-attention element.
Specific family relation. Drawing 'family tree with arrow' is too unspecific (which relation?). Best: 'the son of your brother or sister — my nephew is six years old'.
Specific profession. Drawing 'figure at desk with phone + papers' reads as generic 'office worker'. Best: 'a person who works at a desk — the office clerk answered the phone'.

Idiomatic phrase about supervision. Mime 'pointing to eye then to something' is too vague (could be 'see' or 'watch'). Best: 'watch carefully while doing other things — keep an eye on your little brother'.
Mime: scratch head, look around with dazed face, spin slightly, hands up. Reads as 'confused' at A2+. Risk of collapse to 'don't know'.
Family-relation noun. Drawing 'family tree' is too generic. Best: 'a member of your family — my cousin is my relative'.
Mime: take off imaginary work tie, hand in imaginary briefcase to boss with smile, sit in armchair with feet up. Reads at A2+ from media. Risk of collapse to 'work' or 'tired'.
Time adverb. Same as G3 'immediately'. Mime 'snap fingers + go' is too vague. Best: 'no waiting, now — Come here right away!'
Same as G3. Best: 'get control of something — the new manager took over the company'.
Mime: insert imaginary key into invisible lock, turn it, open door with satisfaction. Reads as 'unlocking' at A2+. Universal.
Mime: hold imaginary handkerchief to face, sniffle, frown deeply, slump shoulders. Reads as 'upset/sad' at A2+. Risk of overlap with 'sad'/'unhappy' — actor adds the snubbing element.
Abstract verb of careful thinking. Mime 'finger to chin' collapses to 'think'. Best: 'think carefully before you decide — please consider my idea'.
Abstract verb (briefly say). Mime 'hand to mouth then quick brush-off' is too vague. Best: 'speak briefly about something — she mentioned the party but didn't give details'.
Modal probability adverb. Mime 'wobble hand back and forth' is too vague. Best: 'probably — it's likely to rain tomorrow'.
Function adverb (in addition). Mime is too vague. Best: 'in addition; also — I'm tired, and besides, it's late'.
Abstract verb of anticipation. Mime 'looking at watch + hopeful face' collapses to 'wait'. Best: 'think something will happen — I expect them to arrive at six'.
Concrete object — small folded square cloth, often white with a pattern at corner. Iconic at A2+. Drawing reads instantly.
Same as G3 'Never mind!'. Mime: wave hand dismissively, smile, shrug. Reads at A2+. Risk of collapse to 'whatever'.
Abstract feeling-noun. Mime 'narrow eyes + side-eye' collapses to 'doubt'. Best: 'a feeling someone did something wrong — the detective had a suspicion about the butler'.
Concrete object — small upright bin with crumpled paper sticking out. Iconic at A2+. Drawing reads instantly.
Intensifier adjective. Mime 'enthusiastic thumbs up + chef-kiss' collapses to 'great'. Best: 'extremely good — the food was excellent'.
Abstract noun (judgement). Mime 'finger up + 'aha!' face' collapses to 'idea'. Best: 'the decision after thinking — what's your conclusion about the case?'

Idiomatic phrasal verb (manage to find/obtain). Mime 'reaching far and grabbing successfully' is plausible but reads as 'grab'. Best: 'manage to find or get — I finally got hold of the book I wanted'.
Abstract verb (show with evidence). Mime 'point at evidence + nod confidently' is plausible but vague. Best: 'show something is true with facts — can you prove that you were there?'
Abstract adjective (about the past). Drawing 'old castle + scroll' is too specific. Best: 'about events long ago — the Battle of Vienna is a historical event'.
Abstract verb (used specifically with crimes/sins). Mime 'do something bad' is too vague. Best: 'to do something bad or illegal — he committed a crime'.
Mime: look around frantically, then run with bag in hand, peek over shoulder, hide behind imaginary wall. Reads as 'getting away' at A2+. Universal.
Abstract noun (process of finding out). Drawing 'magnifying glass + figure' reads as 'detective'. Best: 'finding out what happened, especially a crime — the police started an investigation'.
Polysemous abstract adjective (frequent; ordinary). Mime 'point at lots of things' is too vague. Best: 'happening often or usual — that name is very common in Austria'.
Abstract adjective (private). Mime 'point at self with stop-don't-touch gesture' collapses to 'mine'. Best: 'belonging to a particular person, private — that's a personal letter, don't read it'.
Iconic visual — yellow tape across area, chalk outline of body, footprints. Highly recognizable at A2+ from detective shows. Drawing reads as 'crime scene' instantly.
Same as G3 'to realise'. Mime 'aha! lightbulb' reads at A2+ but collapses to 'idea'. Best: 'suddenly understand — I realised I'd forgotten my keys'.
Mime: rush around frantically, talking on phone while typing on imaginary laptop, juggling tasks. Reads as 'busy' at A2+. Risk of collapse to 'work' — actor adds the chaotic multitasking element.

Abstract concept (style of cooking). Polysemous (also 'kitchen'). Drawing 'plate of food with national flag' is too specific. Best: 'a style of cooking from a country — Italian cuisine is famous for pasta'.
Identity noun. Drawing 'figure with suitcase + welcome sign' reads as 'newcomer' generally. Best: 'a person who comes to live in another country — many immigrants came to America from Europe'.
Abstract adjective (belonging to where born). Mime 'point at ground + self' collapses to 'home'. Best: 'belonging to where you were born — German is her native language'.
Locative adverb. Mime 'point to close-by area' is too vague. Best: 'not far away — there's a park nearby'.
Abstract noun (where something comes from). Mime 'point backward + self' is too vague. Best: 'where something or someone comes from — what's the origin of this story?'
Abstract activity-noun. Drawing 'flag + parliament + people arguing' is vague. Best: 'work and arguments about how a country is run — many adults follow politics'.
Mime: cup hands around mouth like megaphone, mouth important news with formal posture. Reads as 'public statement'. Risk of collapse to 'shout'. Backup: actor includes 'attention please' gesture.
Mime: hold head with worried face, look around helplessly, point at imaginary mess. Reads as 'in trouble'. Risk of collapse to 'sad' or 'worried'.
Mime: place imaginary object, step back with hands over ears, then arms wide with explosion shape, mouth a 'BOOM!'. Universal at A2+ from cartoon contexts.

Compound abstract noun (specific aviation event). Drawing 'plane on field with smoke' is plausible but specific. Best: 'when a plane has to land quickly because of a problem — the captain made an emergency landing'.
Same as G3. Mime: line of people walking quickly out of building, look back at danger. Risk of collapse to 'leave'.
Concrete configuration — many V-shaped bird silhouettes flying together. Iconic at A2+. Drawing reads instantly.
Mime: arms out wide like wings, body slowly tilting downward in smooth controlled motion. Reads as 'gliding' at A2+. Universal.
Same as G3. Best: 'something amazing you can't explain — it's a miracle no one was hurt'.

Idiomatic phrase (currently working). Drawing 'figure in uniform with badge' is plausible but specific to police/military. Best: 'currently working as part of your job — the doctor is on duty until midnight'.
Concrete vehicle — small motorboat, often orange/red, with people being pulled aboard. Iconic at A2+. Drawing reads as 'rescue boat' or 'lifeboat'.
Concrete airport feature — long flat strip with markings, plane on or near it. Iconic at A2+. Drawing reads as 'runway'.

Mime: arms angled up like wings, body leaning forward, slow gradual rising motion. Same handling as G3 'to take off' but as a noun. Risk of overlap with the verb — actor adds the moment-of-departure framing.
Polysemous abstract noun (medical care; behaviour towards). Mime 'doctor putting bandage' captures medical sense but specific. Best: 'medical care for an illness — she got treatment in hospital'.
Concrete physical feature — feathered or aircraft wing in profile. Iconic at A2+. Drawing reads instantly.
Mime: pace anxiously, hands to head, plead with imaginary person, drop to knees. Reads at A2+. Risk of collapse to 'sad' or 'beg'. Backup: actor adds the 'no way out' framing.
Mime: hold two imaginary objects (cars/balls), drive them toward each other, clap hands hard at impact + recoil. Universal at A2+ from physics/sports contexts.
Mime: hold imaginary object, throw arms wide with 'BOOM!' face. Same as 'blow up' but actor distinguishes by emphasising the 'sudden burst' moment without buildup.

Abstract trait noun (related to G3 'brave'). Mime 'heroic chest-out pose' captures the adjective but the noun reads as 'hero'. Best: 'being ready to face danger without fear — her bravery saved them'.
Mime: hand over imaginary medal/prize/money to someone with handshake. Reads as 'giving prize'. Risk of collapse to 'give' or 'prize'.
Same as G3 'critic'. Best: 'someone whose job is to say if a film or song is good — the film critic wrote a review'.
Concrete object — tall narrow box with arrows up/down and number panel. Iconic at A2+. Drawing reads instantly. Show 'standing in tight space miming up arrow' is also possible.
Abstract organised-effort noun. Drawing 'people holding signs marching' reads as 'protest'. Best: 'an organised effort to achieve a goal — they ran a campaign to save the trees'.

Polysemous (also 'attack'; 'electric charge'; 'accuse'). Specifically the 'ask for payment' sense here. Mime 'cash register click + receive money' is plausible but reads as 'sell'. Best: 'ask someone to pay — the shop charges 5 euros for delivery'.

Compound abstract noun (modern concept). Drawing 'many people putting coins in jar' is plausible but vague. Best: 'when many people online give a little money for a project — the campaign used crowd-funding'.
Abstract noun (formal account). Drawing 'paper with text + microphone' reads as 'speech/news'. Best: 'an official account of facts or opinions — the witness gave a statement to the police'.

Profession defined by activity. Drawing 'figure with calculator + ledger + glasses' reads as 'desk worker'. Best: 'a person whose job is to manage money records — the accountant checks the company's finances'.
Mime: stand at imaginary desk, smile, mouth 'good morning, can I help you?' while gesturing. Reads at A2+ from hotel/office contexts. Risk of collapse to 'hello'.
Mime: lie under imaginary car, turn wrench, slide out with greasy hands rubbed on overalls. Reads at A2+. Risk of collapse to 'fixing' — actor adds the under-car position.
Mime: take pulse on imaginary wrist, hold thermometer to forehead, write on chart with caring face. Reads at A2+. Risk of collapse to 'doctor' — actor adds the bedside-care framing.
Abstract compound noun (services). Drawing 'hospital + doctor + medicine' is too generic. Best: 'medical services for sick people — Austria has good health care'.
Abstract business activity. Drawing 'megaphone + product' reads as 'advertising'. Best: 'work of selling and promoting products — she works in marketing for a phone company'.
Abstract financial-management noun. Drawing 'piles of money + calculator' is too vague. Best: 'work of managing money — the bank's finance department checks all the accounts'.
Mime: pretend to strip wires with imaginary pliers, plug in lightbulb that lights up, then test with imaginary multimeter. Reads at A2+. Risk of collapse to 'fixing'.

Mime: type at imaginary keyboard, answer imaginary phone with one hand, sort papers with the other. Reads as 'office worker'. Risk of overlap with 'office clerk' — actor adds the answering-phone element.
Mime: walk slowly down an aisle, demonstrate seatbelt + oxygen mask + emergency exit gestures. The pre-flight safety mime is iconic at A2+. Risk of collapse to 'plane'.
Abstract field-noun. Drawing 'computer with code on screen' is too specific. Best: 'using computers to handle information — she studies computing at university'.
Compound abstract noun (business area). Mime fails. Best: 'selling products and promoting them — he works in sales and marketing'.
Same as G3. Best: 'have earned something — she deserves a prize for her hard work'.
Abstract adjective (about women). Drawing '♀ symbol or female silhouette' reads but is reductive. Best: 'about women or girls — there are 12 female students in the class'.
Abstract adjective (about men). Drawing '♂ symbol or male silhouette' reads but reductive. Best: 'about men or boys — male and female lions look different'.

Abstract feeling-noun. Mime 'lean back smiling with hands behind head' collapses to 'happy/relaxed'. Best: 'a pleasant feeling when you achieve something — she felt satisfaction after finishing the project'.
Abstract negative compound. Mime 'shrug + empty pockets + sad' reads at A2+ but vague. Best: 'not having a paid job — many people are unemployed during a recession'.
Abstract life-noun. Drawing 'staircase going up with figure' reads as 'success'. Best: 'the series of jobs you have over time — my mum has had a long career as a teacher'.
Idiomatic phrase (very interested in). Mime 'lean forward with bright eyes' collapses to 'interested'. Best: 'very enthusiastic about — I'm keen on photography, I do it every weekend'.
Same as G3. Best: 'be the one who takes care of something — I'm responsible for feeding the cat'.
Concrete-enough — extra money in an envelope, often with star or '+' symbol. Drawing reads as 'extra money/reward'. Risk of collapse to 'money'. Backup: actor adds a 'star' or '+'.
Abstract time-noun. Drawing 'calendar with red circle and clock' is plausible but vague. Best: 'the last day to finish something — the deadline for the homework is Monday'.
Same as G3. Best: 'create something new over time — they developed a new app'.
Mime: do imaginary work motions, then receive money with satisfied smile. Reads as 'getting paid'. Risk of collapse to 'work'. (Same call as G3 'to earn (money)'.)
Mime: hold imaginary new product up high, present it with arms wide, point to imaginary audience clapping. Reads as 'product reveal'. Risk of collapse to 'show' or 'present'.
Set discourse phrase (advantages + disadvantages). Mime 'thumbs up then thumbs down side by side' is plausible but vague. Best: 'good points and bad points — what are the pros and cons of this plan?'
Abstract financial noun. Drawing 'pay slip with euro amount' reads as 'pay'. Best: 'fixed money you get every month for work — her salary is 3,000 euros'.

Polysemous-feeling phrasal verb (invent in your head). Mime 'finger to head + lightbulb appearing' reads at A2+ from cartoon. Risk of collapse to 'idea'. Best: 'create something new in your mind — I thought up a great story'.
Compound abstract noun. Drawing 'clock with arrows from 9 to 5' is plausible but vague. Best: 'the times you are at work — my working hours are 9 to 5'.
Abstract noun (suggestions). Mime 'finger up + speak confidently' collapses to 'tell'. Best: 'suggestions about what to do — my mum gave me advice about my homework'.
Abstract trait-noun. Mime 'climb invisible ladder with determined face' reads at A2+ but vague. Best: 'a strong wish to do something great — her ambition is to be a doctor'.
Polysemous abstract adjective (informal style; relaxed). Drawing 'jeans + t-shirt' captures the dress sense but specific. Best: 'relaxed, not formal — wear casual clothes to the picnic'.
Polysemous (business; companions). Specifically business sense here. Drawing 'building with logo' reads as 'office'. Best: 'a business that makes or sells things — he works at a phone company'.
Mime: stride forward with chest out, smile broadly, give firm handshake to imaginary person. Reads as 'confident' adverbially. Risk of collapse to 'brave'.
Abstract role-noun (company that pays you). Drawing 'figure handing money to worker' reads as 'boss/payment'. Best: 'a person or company that pays people to work — my employer is a hospital'.
Mime: jump excitedly, big eyes, animated hand-gestures, mouth 'yes! great!'. Reads as 'enthusiastic' at A2+. Risk of overlap with 'excited' — actor exaggerates the engaged-leaning posture.
Mime: look directly into imaginary partner's eyes, point at own eyes then theirs, hold the gaze. Reads as 'eye-to-eye' specifically. Universal at A2+ from interview-skills lessons.
Mime: shake hand of imaginary employer, sit down, mouth answers to questions while gesturing nervously. Reads at A2+ from career-skills contexts. Risk of collapse to 'meeting'.
Mime: read imaginary text intensely, close eyes and concentrate, point to head with confident nod. Reads as 'learning by heart'. Risk of collapse to 'remember'.
Polysemous adverb (in a normal way; of course). Mime 'shrug + smile + go-with-the-flow gesture' is too vague. Best: 'in a normal way — naturally, the kids were tired after the long day'.
Abstract plural noun (abilities). Mime 'flex muscle + show off doing things' collapses to specific skills. Best: 'things you can do well — her skills include cooking and drawing'.
Abstract field-noun. Drawing 'figure with notepad + microphone + newspaper' reads as 'reporter'. Best: 'work of writing news — journalism is important for democracy'.
Abstract adjective (man-made). Mime 'hand wave dismissively + plastic gesture' is too vague. Best: 'made by people, not natural — artificial flavours in sweets'.
Abstract adjective (food makes you gain weight). Mime 'eat then expand belly' collapses to 'fat' or 'eat'. Best: 'food that makes you gain weight — chips and cake are very fattening'.
Abstract adjective (makes you feel full). Mime 'eat + pat satisfied stomach' collapses to 'full'. Best: 'food that makes your stomach feel full — pasta is very filling'.
Mime: full-body recoil with hand to mouth, gag, push food away with extreme grimace. Universal at A2+ from cartoon disgust. Stronger than just 'awful'.
Abstract negative adjective (causing harm). Mime 'point at thing + cross-out + sad face' collapses to 'bad'. Best: 'can cause damage — too much sugar is harmful for your teeth'.
Mime: flex muscle, eat imaginary apple with bright smile, jump up and down energetically. Reads as 'healthy/fit' at A2+. Risk of collapse to 'strong'.
Abstract adjective (rich in nutrients). Mime 'eat green vegetable + thumbs up to body' collapses to 'healthy'. Best: 'has the things your body needs — vegetables are nutritious'.
Polysemous abstract adjective (recently made; cool air; new). Drawing 'apple with shine + dewdrop' captures one sense. Best: 'just made or picked, not old — fresh bread from the bakery'.
Mime: take a bite of imaginary food, eyes roll back in pleasure, kiss fingertips ('chef's kiss'). Iconic at A2+ from cooking-show contexts. Universal.
Identity noun (no meat). Drawing 'plate with no meat + leaves' is plausible. Best: 'a person who doesn't eat meat or fish — my sister is a vegetarian'.
Abstract financial verb. Mime 'check empty wallet, sad face' collapses to 'no money'. Best: 'have enough money to pay — I can't afford a new bike'.
Mime: hold imaginary spoon to baby/animal mouth, lift food carefully, smile encouragingly. Reads as 'feeding' at A2+. Universal.

Mime: hold stomach with weak face, mouth 'I'm starving', mime grabbing for food. Reads as 'hungry/hunger'. Risk of overlap with G3 'thirst' or 'thirsty' — actor uses food-grabbing not throat-clutching.
Abstract noun (amount consumed). Drawing 'arrow into body' is too vague. Best: 'the amount of food or drink you have — your daily salt intake should be small'.
Same as G3 — mime throwing good food away. Risk of collapse to 'rubbish'. Best mime: pretend to scrape full plate into bin with sad face.
Abstract verb (have inside). Mime 'open box + look inside + point' is too vague. Best: 'have something inside — this drink contains lots of sugar'.
Abstract field-noun. Drawing 'pot + utensils + apron' reads as 'cooking'. Best: 'the art of cooking — she takes a cookery class on Saturdays'.
Polysemous (regular eating; weight-loss programme). Drawing 'plate of food' is too vague. Best: 'the food you eat regularly — a balanced diet has lots of vegetables'.
Conjunction. Same as G3. Best: 'although — even though it was raining, we went outside'.
Abstract noun (state of wellness). Drawing 'body + heart + plus sign' reads as 'medical'. Best: 'your body's wellness — taking care of your health is important'.
Abstract process-noun (eating well). Mime 'eat vegetable + thumbs up' collapses to 'eat well'. Best: 'eating the right food for your body — good nutrition helps kids grow'.
Abstract adjective (heavier than healthy). Mime 'puff cheeks and stomach' is potentially insensitive in classroom. Best: 'heavier than healthy — being overweight can cause health problems'.
Adverb of frequency. Mime 'point at clock + repeat gesture' is too vague. Best: 'often, again and again — I exercise regularly, three times a week'.
Mime: turn away from imaginary food, push it away with frown, shake head. Reads at A2+ as 'don't like'. Risk of collapse to 'bad'.
Abstract plural noun (regular actions). Mime 'repeat same action + shrug' is too vague. Best: 'things you do often without thinking — brushing your teeth is a good habit'.
Same as G3 'to accept'. Best: 'say yes to something or take what is given — she accepted the gift'.
Time adverb. Same as G3. Best: 'the time after — we eat dinner, and afterwards we watch TV'.

Specific compound abstract noun (mental health condition). Mime is potentially upsetting in classroom. Best: 'a serious problem with how you eat, often a mental health issue — eating disorders need professional help'.

Polysemous (gain weight; gain knowledge; gain a victory). Specifically the 'gain weight' sense per definition. Mime 'arrow up + point at body' is too vague. Best: 'increase in weight or amount — I gained two kilos over the holidays'.
Concrete location — building with weights, treadmills, sometimes mirror walls. Iconic at A2+. Drawing reads instantly.

Mime: pinch sides showing little space, body posture narrow. Risk of insensitivity in classroom (avoid pointing at students). Drawing 'silhouette comparison' is also possible. Show with self-pinching gesture works at A2+.
Mime: hand to mouth with sick face, body lurches forward, mouth open in 'bleurgh' shape. Visceral and unmistakable at A2+ from media.
Mime: cover face with hands, look down, peek through fingers. Reads as 'ashamed/embarrassed' at A2+. Risk of overlap with 'embarrassed' — actor adds the 'guilty' element with mouth wince.
Abstract relational verb. Mime 'put hand on shoulder + look in eyes confidently' collapses to 'friend'. Best: 'believe someone is honest — I trust my best friend with my secrets'.
Abstract verb (succeed after effort). Mime 'climb to top + arms up in victory' collapses to 'win'. Best: 'succeed after working hard — she achieved her goal of running a marathon'.
Mime: hold imaginary money/food/clothes, drop into imaginary collection box, look at it with kind face. Reads as 'giving to charity'. Risk of collapse to 'give'.
Idiomatic phrasal verb (quit before finishing). Mime 'school bag thrown down, walk away' is plausible but specific. Best: 'leave school before finishing — she dropped out at 16 to start a band'.

Polysemous (goal in football; goal in life). Drawing 'football goal with ball' captures sport sense; arrow at target captures abstract sense. Best in words to handle the life-goal sense: 'something you want to achieve — my goal is to learn Spanish'.
Abstract financial noun. Drawing 'arrow into wallet' is plausible but vague. Best: 'money that you earn or get regularly — the family's income comes from both parents working'.
Abstract verb (give desire). Mime 'lightbulb above someone's head from your action' is too narrative. Best: 'make someone want to do great things — her speech inspired me to study harder'.
Same as G3. Best: 'help someone or give them what they need — my parents support me when I'm stressed'.
Abstract noun (giving confidence). Mime 'pat on back + thumbs up + smile' collapses to 'good job'. Best: 'words that give someone confidence — my coach gave me lots of encouragement before the game'.
Same as G3. Best: 'people who live in the same area or share something — our school community is friendly'.
Abstract verb (go beyond). Mime 'arrow above limit + raised hand' is too vague. Best: 'do more than expected — her grades exceeded what the teacher hoped for'.
Mime: hands to head pulling at hair, growl through teeth, stomp foot, throw imaginary papers. Universal at A2+ from cartoon contexts. Strong body language.
Mime: hands together in 'thank you' bow, hand over heart, big smile, nod head deeply. Reads as 'thankful' at A2+. Risk of collapse to 'thank you'.
Function phrase (especially). Mime 'point at one thing in a group with emphasis' is too vague. Best: 'especially, more than others — I love fruit, in particular strawberries'.
Idiomatic phrase (gain wisdom from experience). Mime 'finger up + nod knowingly' is too vague. Best: 'understand something better after a mistake — I learned a lesson: never lie to my mum'.
Function phrase (a variety of). Mime 'arms wide showing many different things' is plausible but vague. Best: 'a variety of — the shop has a range of bikes for different ages'.

Abstract idiomatic verb (understand someone's feelings). Mime 'point at self then at other + nod sympathetically' collapses to 'agree'. Best: 'understand because you've felt the same way — I can relate to her, I was nervous on my first day too'.
Set discourse phrase. Mime 'shrug + eye-roll + 'of course' face' is too vague. Best: 'a way to say it's not surprising — Small wonder he's tired, he played football all day'.

Polysemous abstract verb (send signal; pass disease). Mime 'wave from one hand to another + radio dial' is too vague. Best: 'send something from one place to another — radios transmit music through the air'.

Specific identity noun (Indigenous Australian). Drawing 'figure with body paint + boomerang' risks stereotype/insensitivity. Best: 'a person from the group who first lived in Australia — Aborigines have lived there for tens of thousands of years'.
Concrete object — rectangular paper with bank logo, signature line, amount in numbers + words. Iconic at A2+. Drawing reads instantly.
Concrete object — rectangle with flap closure, often with stamp at corner. Iconic at A2+. Drawing reads instantly.
Abstract company-noun. Drawing 'plane with logo + sign' is plausible but vague. Best: 'a company that runs flights — Austrian Airlines is an airline'.
Family-relation noun (relative from long ago). Drawing 'family tree going back many generations' is plausible but slow. Best: 'a person in your family from long ago — my ancestors lived in Spain'.
Concrete path-noun. Drawing 'narrow winding path through scrub bushes' reads as 'path in nature'. Risk of overlap with G3 'path'. Backup: actor adds Australian-style scrub vegetation.
Mime: drop to hands and knees, move forward slowly. Same as G3 'to crawl low' but without the specific fire-safety context. Universal at A2+.
Mime: grasp imaginary heavy object with both hands behind you, lean forward and pull along the ground with strain. Reads as 'dragging' at A2+. Universal.

Specific aviation context (luggage too heavy). Mime 'lift huge suitcase + struggle + airline staff shake head' is plausible but specific. Best: 'luggage heavier than the airline allows — you have to pay for excess weight'.
Intensifier adjective (extremely beautiful). Mime 'jaw drop + chef's kiss' collapses to 'beautiful'. Best: 'extremely beautiful — what a gorgeous sunset!'
Mime: extend arm quickly, snatch imaginary object, pull it close to chest. Reads as 'grabbing' at A2+. Universal.
Concrete car part — round bright light on front of car, sometimes shown with rays. Iconic at A2+. Drawing reads instantly.

Abstract cultural noun. Drawing 'old castle + family + traditional dress' is too specific. Best: 'the traditions and culture from your country's past — the Vienna State Opera is part of Austria's heritage'.
Specific procedure (connect car batteries). Mime 'open imaginary bonnet + connect cables + listen + smile when engine starts' reads at A2+ from car-trouble contexts. Risk of collapse to 'fix car'.
Same as G3 — polysemous (physical; mental stress). Best: 'when something pushes against something — there's a lot of pressure to finish on time'.
Same as G3 — could draw figure under tree but reads as 'tree'. Best: 'an area not in direct sun — let's sit in the shade'.
Concrete physical object — thin twisted line, sometimes tied around a parcel. Iconic at A2+. Drawing reads as 'string/twine'.
Concrete plant — tall thin grass with feathery top, growing in water. Iconic at A2+ from nature contexts. Risk of collapse to 'grass'. Backup: actor draws water at base.

Polysemous (animal track; running track; railway track). Specifically the 'mark on ground' sense per definition. Drawing 'paw prints in mud' reads as 'animal track'. Best: 'marks left on the ground — the hunters followed the animal's tracks'.
Abstract compound noun. Drawing 'fire + shelter + water gathering' is too narrative. Best: 'things you can do to stay alive in nature — survival skills include making fire'.
Specific cultural-context noun. Mime 'walk a long way alone with bag' reads as 'hiking' generically. Best: 'a long journey on foot in the Australian bush, traditionally done by Aboriginal people'.
Concrete vehicle — generic plane silhouette with wings + tail. Iconic at A2+. Drawing reads instantly.
Concrete vehicle — white van/truck with red cross or red stripes, sometimes with siren-light on top. Iconic at A2+. Drawing reads instantly.
Abstract adjective (with lots of small facts). Mime 'point at imaginary text + zoom in' is too vague. Best: 'with lots of small information — she gave a detailed description'.
Abstract measurement noun. Drawing 'two points with arrow showing space' is plausible but vague. Best: 'the space between two places — what's the distance from here to Vienna?'
Polysemous (medicine; illegal substances). Drawing 'pill bottle + tablets' captures the medicine sense per definition. Risk of collapse to 'medicine'. Backup: actor draws prescription label.
Iconic — green/white cross box with bandages + plasters spilling out. Universally recognizable at A2+. Drawing reads as 'first aid kit' instantly.
Mime: arms outstretched then slowly lowering, feet touching down with a small bend. Mirror of G3 'to take off' / 'to land'. Universal at A2+.
Specific geographic concept — vast red dirt landscape with sparse vegetation, often with kangaroo or boab tree. Iconic at A2+ from media. Drawing reads as 'Australian outback'.
Abstract giving-verb. Mime 'hand over many things to someone' collapses to 'give'. Best: 'give someone what they need — the school provides books for all students'.
Specific abstract concept (illegal trade). Drawing 'shadowy figure with dollar bills' is too vague and stereotyped. Best: 'illegal selling of forbidden things — they bought it on the black market'.
Mime: pick up imaginary objects one by one and place into imaginary box, gesture 'one more!' eagerly. Reads as 'gathering' at A2+. Universal.
Same as G3. Best: 'lots of things you have gathered — my brother has a collection of football cards'.
Abstract feeling-noun. Mime 'wide eyes + lean forward intently' collapses to 'interested'. Best: 'a very strong interest in something — her fascination with space made her become an astronaut'.
Abstract adjective (uncommon). Mime 'show only one finger + point to small space' is too vague. Best: 'not seen often — pandas are very rare animals'.
Mime: hold imaginary gavel, point at imaginary bidders raising paddles, slam gavel on stand calling 'sold!'. Reads at A2+ from media. Risk of collapse to 'sale'.

Mime: pretend something is on fire (waving fire-fingers around imaginary structure), then slowly collapse it down with both hands as it disappears. Reads as 'destroyed by fire'. Risk of collapse to 'fire'.
