Polysemous (act of copying; an instance of a book). Specifically the noun 'one instance' here. Drawing 'two identical books side by side' reads as 'same'. Best: 'one example of a book or paper — there are many copies of this book in the library'.
Specific abstract verb (kill as punishment). Mime is upsetting in classroom. Best: 'kill someone as a legal punishment — long ago, criminals were executed by hanging'.
Mime: red face (puff cheeks), clench fists, stomp foot, shout silently with veins-popping face. Stronger than 'angry' — exaggerated. Universal at A2+.
Iconic visual — figure in black robe with white wig and gavel, sitting elevated. Recognizable at A2+ from media. Risk of collapse to 'wig' or 'lawyer'. Backup: actor draws gavel prominently.

Profession. Drawing 'figure with glasses behind library counter, finger to lips shushing' is plausible but reads as generic 'quiet worker'. Best: 'a person who works in a library helping people find books'.
Concrete location — building/room with rows of bookshelves, often with reading tables. Iconic at A2+. Drawing reads instantly.
Concrete building — old stone building with cross/bell tower, often with monks visible. Iconic at A2+ from history contexts. Risk of collapse to 'church' — actor adds the multi-residence framing.
Iconic visual — figure in brown robe with shaved head/tonsure, often with rope belt. Recognizable at A2+. Drawing reads as 'monk'.
Abstract value-adjective. Mime 'hold imaginary tiny thing carefully + sparkle gesture' collapses to 'beautiful'. Best: 'very valuable or important — her grandmother's ring is precious to her'.

Abstract verb (keep in good condition). Mime 'wrap something carefully + put in box + close lid' is plausible but reads as 'pack'. Best: 'keep something in its original state — we should preserve nature for the future'.
Mime: enter imaginary bank with mask on, point fingers like gun, demand bag of money, run out. Reads at A2+ from cartoon. Risk of overlap with 'to steal' — actor adds the bank/forced element.
Multi-word legal phrase. Mime is upsetting in classroom. Best: 'a court orders that someone must be killed — in some countries, criminals can be sentenced to death'.
Mime: hold imaginary string/stick with both hands wide apart, then bring hands closer together. Reads as 'making shorter'. Risk of collapse to 'small'.
Identity noun (person dependent). Mime is sensitive in classroom. Best: 'a person who can't stop doing something harmful — chocolate addict, video game addict'.
Abstract condition-noun. Drawing/mime fails. Best: 'when you can't stop doing something harmful — phone addiction is a problem for many teens'.

Polysemous (military order; computer command; verbal order). Mime 'point firmly with stern face' collapses to 'no'. Best: 'an order from someone in authority — the captain gave the soldiers a command'.
Mime: spin around with arms flailing, eyes rolled, mouth in chaotic shout, hold head as if losing it. Reads as 'going crazy/wild' at A2+ from cartoon. Universal.
Mime: see something fun happen across the room, reach toward it sadly as it ends, slap forehead with regret. Reads as 'missing' at A2+. Risk of collapse to 'sad'.
Mime: touch own face/cheeks with worried look, sway as if dizzy, near-faint. The 'blood drained' look reads at A2+. Risk of collapse to 'sick' — actor avoids stomach-clutching.
Mime: enter dramatically through imaginary door, surprised wave hello, point at watch as if to say 'finally here'. Reads as 'arriving (often late)' at A2+. Risk of collapse to 'come'.
Same as G3. Iconic mime — hand cupped beside mouth, lean toward listener, mouth words very small. Universal at A2+.

Polysemous (single piece of paper; bedsheet). Per definition the paper sense. Drawing 'A4 piece of paper, single' reads as 'paper'. Best: 'a single piece of paper — write your name on a sheet of paper'.
Mime: speak rapidly with confusing gestures while imaginary person looks puzzled and head-scratches. Reads at A2+. Risk of collapse to 'confused' (the patient, not the agent).
Abstract aesthetic adjective. Drawing 'overly decorated colourful object' is plausible but vague. Best: 'too colourful, sentimental, or cheap-looking — those plastic flowers are really kitschy'.
Concrete clothing — long white gown with veil, often poofy skirt. Iconic at A2+. Drawing reads instantly.
Concrete clothing — formal black suit with bow tie or boutonnière. Risk of collapse to 'suit' from G3. Backup: actor adds the bow tie + boutonnière.
Iconic visual — woman in white wedding dress, often with veil + bouquet. Recognizable at A2+. Drawing reads instantly.
Iconic visual — man in wedding suit, often next to bride. Drawing reads as 'groom' at A2+. Risk of collapse to 'groom' or 'man in suit'.
Specific wedding role. Drawing 'woman in matching dress next to bride' reads as 'wedding scene'. Best: 'a girl or woman who helps the bride at her wedding'.
Same as G3. Concrete geographic feature — line on map or fence with flagged territories. Drawing reads as 'border' at A2+.
Same as G3 — mime gesturing wildly + mouth words + signal with hands. Risk of collapse to 'to talk'.
Mime: pose like model, hand on hip, swirl as if showing off outfit, smile knowingly. Reads as 'stylish' at A2+. Risk of collapse to 'pretty/elegant'.
Discourse marker. Mime 'finger up #1' is too vague. Best: 'used to introduce the first point — Firstly, I want to thank you all'.
Specific ceremony noun. Drawing 'gravestone + figures in black' is sensitive in classroom. Best: 'a ceremony after someone dies — they had a funeral for grandpa last week'.
Compound abstract noun. Mime 'point at thing + cross-out + body' is too vague. Best: 'something that could harm your body — smoking is a serious health risk'.
Function phrase (shared). Mime 'point at A then B + connect with hand' is too vague. Best: 'shared by two or more — we have a lot in common, we both love football'.
Concrete object — thin sharp metal pin, often with thread through eye. Iconic at A2+. Drawing reads instantly.
Abstract adjective (lasting). Mime 'fixed gesture + forever sweep' is too vague. Best: 'lasting forever — a tattoo is permanent, you can't easily remove it'.
Mime: pinch ear/eyebrow with shock at imaginary needle, then point to small jewel in nose/ear with proud face. Same handling as G2 'to get a nose stud'. Risk of collapse to 'piercing'.
Mime: stand defiantly with arms crossed, sneer, shake head 'no' angrily, rip up imaginary rule paper. Reads at A2+. Risk of collapse to 'angry'.
Abstract belief-adjective. Drawing 'cross + church + praying figure' is too narrow (Christianity only). Best: 'believing in a religion — my grandma is very religious, she goes to church every week'.
Abstract event-noun. Drawing 'altar + figures in formal dress' is too specific. Best: 'a formal event for an important occasion — the wedding ceremony lasts an hour'.

Mime: hold imaginary shovel, dig hole, place imaginary thing in ground, fill hole, pat earth flat. Reads at A2+ as 'burying'. Risk of association with funerals — actor can use treasure-buried framing.
Iconic visual — figure with horns, pointed tail, pitchfork, often red. Universally recognizable at A2+ from cartoon. Drawing reads instantly.
Mime: scratch head, look around with dazed face, hands up in 'what?' gesture. Same as G3 'confusion' (noun). Universal at A2+.
Specific geographic concept. Drawing 'map of Asia with arrow at China/Japan' is plausible but reads as 'Asia'. Best: 'eastern Asian countries — China, Japan, and Korea are in the Far East'.
Mime: make many different hand-gestures in sequence (wave, thumbs up, peace sign, OK sign), then point to hands. Reads as 'gesture' at A2+. Universal.
Mime: wave hello, smile broadly, mouth 'hi!' or 'hello!', extend hand for handshake. Reads as 'greeting' at A2+. Universal.
Concrete body part — labelled hand showing the pointing finger. Iconic at A2+. Drawing reads as 'index finger' specifically.
Mime: stick out tongue at imaginary person, mouth rude words, point and laugh. Reads at A2+ from playground contexts. Risk of collapse to 'rude'.
Mime: nod head emphatically up and down with smile. Universal at A2+. Same handling as G3 'to agree'.
Concrete body part — open hand showing palm side, fingers spread. Iconic at A2+. Drawing reads instantly.
Mime: receive imaginary item from one person on left, turn to person on right, hand over to them. Reads as 'passing along' at A2+.
Concrete body part — thumb sticking out from fist, often with 'thumbs up' framing. Iconic at A2+. Drawing reads instantly.
Abstract noun (act of winning). Mime 'arms up + cheer + V-sign' collapses to 'win' or 'happy'. Best: 'when you win a battle or game — victory in the championship was their dream'.
Concrete number/symbol — '0' digit, often with line through it (∅). Iconic at A2+. Drawing reads instantly.
Compound adjective. Mime 'look at imaginary person + thumbs sideways/medium-OK gesture' collapses to 'OK'. Best: 'pleasant to look at, OK-good — he's a decent-looking guy'.
Mime: cheeks turn red (cover face), look down and away, fidget with shirt, peek through fingers. Universal at A2+ from many shared contexts. (Same as G2 'embarrassed'.)
Mime: hand to mouth covering it, shoulders shake, body wiggle, mouth 'hee hee hee' with eyes scrunched. Reads as 'silly laugh' at A2+.

Specific subculture identity. Drawing 'figure dressed in black + black makeup + dark clothes' reads at A2+ from media. Risk of stereotype — actor includes specific elements (black lipstick, dyed hair).
Mime: rush with rapid movements, fumble things, look at watch with panic, do tasks badly because hurrying. Reads as 'in a hurry' at A2+.
Same as G3. Mime: turn head pointedly, look the other way with arms crossed. Universal at A2+ from playground contexts.
Mime: take big breath in, then exhale with slumped shoulders, eye-roll, hand to forehead. Reads as 'sigh' at A2+. Universal.
Concrete location — couch + TV + coffee table + lamp. Iconic at A2+. Drawing reads as 'living room/sitting room' instantly.
Mime: jump out at imaginary creature shouting 'BOO!' with arms wide, watch it run away with smug face. Reads at A2+. Risk of overlap with 'chase away' from G3.
Concrete clothing part — arm of a shirt/jacket in profile, separate from main body. Iconic at A2+. Drawing reads instantly.
Abstract noun (something that might happen). Mime 'wobble hand + maybe gesture' is too vague. Best: 'something that might happen — there's a possibility of rain tomorrow'.
Concrete substance — black liquid pumping from a pump-jack/oil rig, or in a barrel. Iconic at A2+. Drawing reads instantly.
Specific abstract economic concept. Drawing 'logo + handshake' is too unspecific. Best: 'a system that pays farmers a fair price — Fair Trade chocolate helps farmers in poor countries'.
Iconic visual — figure with overalls + hat, holding pitchfork or rake, near barn/animals. Recognizable at A2+. Drawing reads instantly.
Idiomatic phrase. Mime 'work + receive money + use for food/rent' is too narrative. Best: 'earn enough money for what you need — it's hard to make a living as a poet'.
Compound abstract noun. Drawing 'arrow up + money' reads at A2+ but vague. Best: 'when your salary goes up — she got a pay rise after a year of good work'.
Concrete substance — bottle/spray with skull symbol or 'X' over insect. Drawing reads as 'bug poison' at A2+. Risk of collapse to 'poison' from G3.
Mime: look at imaginary group of options carefully, then point at one with confident nod. Reads as 'choosing'. Risk of collapse to 'choose' or 'point'.

Abstract noun (arrangement). Mime 'two people shake hands after discussion' reads as 'shake hands' or 'meeting'. Best: 'an arrangement made between two people — they made an agreement to share the work'.
Mime: hand at low position, slowly rise it up to high position with widening gesture. Reads as 'going up'. Risk of collapse to 'big' or 'up'.
Polysemous (speed; ratio; price level). Mime 'dial gauge with arrow' is too vague. Best: 'how fast or how much — the rate of climate change is increasing'.
Specific family relation. Drawing 'family tree' is too generic. Best: 'the brother of your wife or husband, or your sister's husband'.
Mime: pretend boxing match — hit + win pose with arms up over fallen imaginary opponent. Reads as 'beat/defeat' at A2+. Risk of collapse to 'win' or 'fight'.
Abstract noun (peaceful agreement). Mime 'people holding hands in circle smiling' reads as 'friends'. Best: 'when people get along peacefully — the family lives in harmony'.
Abstract noun (a person). Drawing 'figure with arrow labelled human' is plausible but vague. Best: 'a man, woman, or child — every human being deserves respect'.
Abstract emotional adjective. Mime 'say something + other person flinches and tears up' is plausible but reads as 'mean'. Best: 'causing emotional pain — his words were really hurtful'.
Abstract noun (lack of knowledge). Mime 'shrug + don't-know face' collapses to 'don't know'. Best: 'not knowing or understanding something — racism comes from ignorance'.

Abstract verb (succeed despite difficulty). Mime 'climb obstacle with effort + arms up at top' reads at A2+ but vague. Best: 'succeed in dealing with a problem — she overcame her fear of public speaking'.
Same as G3. Mime: clutch a body part, scrunched face, sharp inhale. Pain-face is universal at A2+.
Specific abstract social concept. Drawing fails. Best: 'unfair treatment because of someone's race — racism is wrong and harmful'.
Specific abstract adjective/noun. Best: 'showing unfair treatment because of race — that comment was racist'.

Polysemous (acknowledgement; identification). Specifically the praise sense per definition. Mime 'pat on back + nod proudly' collapses to 'good job'. Best: 'being praised for something — she got recognition for her hard work'.
Specific abstract historical concept. Drawing fails (sensitive). Best: 'the system of owning people and forcing them to work — slavery was abolished long ago'.
Specific family relation. Drawing 'family tree' is too generic. Best: 'the husband of your daughter'.
Mime: red face, clenched fists, stomping foot, sharp shouts (silent). Universal at A2+. (Risk of overlap with 'furious' from Unit 8 — actor uses less-extreme version.)
Mime: do something repetitive and irritating to imaginary person (poke them, hum loudly), watch them get more frustrated. Reads at A2+. Risk of collapse to 'angry'.
Mime: hands up in 'I can't do anything!' gesture, look around desperately, drop to knees. Reads at A2+. Risk of collapse to 'sad' or 'don't know'.
Polysemous (physical hurt; emotional hurt). Mime: grab hurt body part with wince. Same as 'painful' but verb form. Risk of duplication — actor uses elbow-bump motion.
Abstract negative compound (not interpreted correctly). Mime is too narrative. Best: 'when people don't understand you correctly — she felt misunderstood by her parents'.
Mime: chest puffed out, beaming smile, hand on heart, gesture at imaginary achievement (medal/child). Reads at A2+. Risk of collapse to 'happy'.
Same as G3. Mime: hands fly to face, jaw drops wide, eyes huge, take a step back. Universal at A2+ from cartoon.
Mime: jump in surprise with eyes wide, hand to chest, mouth open in 'oh!'. Universal at A2+. Distinct from 'shocked' (which has the upset element).
Abstract verb (assert). Mime 'point firmly + serious face + 'I say so'' collapses to 'say'. Best: 'say something is true (without proof) — he claims he can speak five languages'.
Concrete vehicle — two wheels with frame + handlebars + pedals + seat. Iconic at A2+. Drawing reads instantly.
Abstract trait noun. Mime 'scales balanced equally' is plausible but vague. Best: 'treating people equally and reasonably — fairness is important in sport'.
Polysemous (religious; figurative bad situation). Drawing 'flames + devil' reads as 'fire' or 'devil'. Best: 'a place of punishment in some religions, or a really bad situation — that exam was hell'.
Abstract noun (first part). Mime 'open imaginary book + point to first page' is plausible but vague. Best: 'the first part of a book or speech — the introduction tells you what's coming next'.
Concrete environmental scene — smoke from factory, plastic in river, dirty air. Drawing reads at A2+. Risk of collapse to 'rubbish' or 'smoke'.
Same as G3 'script'. Drawing 'bound pages with character names + dialogue lines' reads as 'script'. Best: 'the written text of a film with the dialogue — the screenplay won an award'.
Same call as G3. Polysemous (verb 'to play' vs noun 'theatre play'). Best: 'a story performed by actors on stage — we saw a play at the school theatre'.
Abstract literary form. Drawing 'page with verse + heart symbol' is too narrow. Best: 'writing with rhythm and feelings — poetry is about expressing emotions'.
Concrete object — book with grid of panels showing pictures + speech bubbles. Iconic at A2+. Drawing reads instantly.
Specific abstract noun (collected works). Drawing 'thick book with many authors' reads as 'book'. Best: 'a collection of poems or stories chosen by an editor'.
Concrete object — thick book labelled 'A-Z', often with sample word + definition visible. Iconic at A2+. Drawing reads instantly.
Concrete object — book with title + author. Risk of collapse to 'book' generally. Backup: actor draws title page indicating fiction.
Specific book-type. Drawing 'book with figure on cover' reads as 'book'. Best: 'a book about someone's life — I read a biography of Steve Jobs'.
Specific literary form (brief fiction). Mime 'small book + small gesture' is too vague. Best: 'a brief story, shorter than a novel — the magazine has three short stories this month'.
Compound abstract noun. Drawing 'newspaper with star ratings + book' is plausible but specific. Best: 'a written opinion about a book — I read a book review in the paper'.
Concrete physical barrier — vertical posts with horizontal rails or chain-link, often around a yard. Iconic at A2+. Drawing reads instantly.
Polysemous abstract adjective (not guilty; naive). Mime 'angelic face + halo gesture' reads as 'angel/good'. Best: 'not guilty of a crime — the judge said he was innocent'.
Same as G3. Mime: open imaginary present with eager face, then deflate with sad face and shoulders down. Risk of collapse to 'sad'.
Same as G3. Best: 'like one thing more than another — I prefer tea to coffee'.
Specific publishing term. Drawing 'back cover of book with description' is plausible but specific. Best: 'short description on the back of a book — I read the blurb before buying it'.
Iconic visual — figure with top hat, monocle, money bag with $ symbol, fancy clothes. Drawing reads at A2+ from cartoon. Risk of collapse to 'rich'.
Iconic visual — small figure with butterfly wings, dress, magic wand, often with sparkles. Universal at A2+ from media. Drawing reads instantly.
Specific compound book-type. Mime fails. Best: 'a long story set in the past — Outlander is a historical novel set in Scotland'.
Polysemous abstract noun (mention; source). Mime 'point at imaginary book then back to text' is too vague. Best: 'a mention or connection to something — the song has a reference to her childhood'.
Concrete configuration — three books stacked or side-by-side, labelled '1', '2', '3'. Drawing reads at A2+ from media (Lord of the Rings etc.). Risk of collapse to 'books'.

rows.justification: Mime: pretend to hear knock/bell, get up and walk to imaginary door, open it with curious face. Reads at A2+. Universal.
Mime: pick up imaginary clutter, sweep, wipe surfaces, look around with satisfied tidy nod. Reads as 'tidying up' at A2+.
Concrete object — two round/oval lenses joined by a strap, fitting over eyes (swim or lab style). Iconic at A2+. Drawing reads instantly.
Iconic visual — figure (often man) wearing tartan plaid skirt, often with sporran + knee-high socks. Universal at A2+ from Scottish culture references. Drawing reads instantly.
Idiomatic phrase (organise life). Mime is too narrative. Best: 'organise your life or solve problems — I need to sort myself out before the new term'.
Idiomatic British phrase (small problem). Mime 'small worried gesture' is too vague. Best: 'a small problem — I had a spot of bother with my computer this morning'.

Polysemous (Scottish/Irish 'small'; childish term for urine). Per definition the 'tiny' sense. Mime 'pinch fingers showing tiny size' reads as 'small' generally. Best: 'very small (Scottish/Irish English) — there's a wee mouse in the garden'.
Mime: receive imaginary command from authority figure, salute, do what was asked promptly. Reads at A2+. Risk of collapse to 'follow' or 'do'.
Mime: rub fingernails repeatedly on arm/back/head with relieved face. Universal at A2+. Iconic from itchy contexts.
Concrete space object — irregular rocky lump in space, often surrounded by stars. Iconic at A2+ from astronomy contexts. Drawing reads instantly.
Iconic visual — figure in white spacesuit + helmet with reflective visor, often floating with backpack. Universal at A2+. Drawing reads instantly.

Same as Unit 3 'explode' but as noun. Mime: throw arms wide with 'BOOM!' face, then look at imaginary debris. Risk of overlap with 'blow up' / 'explode' — actor uses noun-framing (point at imaginary explosion).
Concrete physical concept — planet with elliptical/circular path drawn around it, often with another body on the path. Drawing reads at A2+. Risk of collapse to 'circle'.
Concrete object — rectangular metal plate with engraved text on a wall. Drawing reads at A2+. Risk of collapse to 'sign' — actor adds wall-mounted framing.
Iconic visual — distinctive orbiter shape with delta wings + booster rockets attached. Recognizable at A2+ from media. Drawing reads instantly.
Adverb (in total). Mime 'sum-up gesture with hands together' is too vague. Best: 'in total — there are 30 students altogether'.
Polysemous (planet's gases; mood/feeling). Drawing 'planet with curved layer of air around it' captures the science sense. Best: 'the layer of gases around a planet — Earth's atmosphere protects us'.
Abstract group-noun. Drawing 'figures in matching uniforms together' reads as 'team'. Best: 'a group of people who work together on a ship or spacecraft — the space shuttle crew of seven'.
Mime: full-body recoil with hand to mouth, gag, push food away with extreme grimace. Same as 'revolting' from Unit 5 — actor varies by stronger throat-gag for 'disgusting'.
Abstract field-noun. Drawing 'figure with hard hat + blueprints + bridge' reads as 'building'. Best: 'designing and building machines or bridges — engineering helped us go to space'.
Abstract collective noun (all humans). Drawing 'many figures in a circle' reads as 'people/group'. Best: 'all humans together — going to the moon was a step for all mankind'.
Abstract activity-noun. Drawing 'rocket + planets + astronaut' reads as 'space' generically. Best: 'going into space — space travel will be possible for tourists soon'.
Concrete natural phenomenon — half-circle of sun rising over horizon, often with rays/colours. Iconic at A2+. Drawing reads instantly.
Concrete natural phenomenon — sun half-visible at horizon, often with reddish sky. Iconic at A2+. Drawing reads as 'sunset'. Risk of overlap with sunrise — actor adds darkening sky.
Concrete sign — yellow/red triangle with exclamation mark, or 'CAUTION' text. Iconic at A2+. Risk of overlap with 'dangerous' — actor adds explicit text or different layout.
Concrete object — rectangle with bold text + product image + price + 'BUY NOW!'. Iconic at A2+. Drawing reads as 'advertisement'.
Concrete vehicle — rocket/saucer with windows and rocket flame from base. Iconic at A2+. Drawing reads instantly. Risk of overlap with 'space shuttle' — actor draws generic spaceship.

Polysemous (about commerce; TV advertisement). Per definition the 'about commerce' adjective sense. Drawing fails. Best: 'about buying and selling for profit — this is a commercial product, it costs money'.
Mime: stand sternly with hand out, point firmly while mouthing 'NOW!', impatient face. Reads as 'demanding' at A2+. Risk of collapse to 'angry' or 'ask'.
Compound number-prefix. Drawing 'huge stack of money' reads as 'lots of money'. Best: 'involving billions — a multibillion-dollar company'.
Compound abstract phrase. Drawing fails. Best: 'belonging to a private company or person, not the government — SpaceX is privately owned'.
Same as G3. Mime: fist-pump, party dance, blow horn, cheer with arms in air. Universal at A2+.
Mime: slump shoulders, drag feet, sad far-away face, slump in chair, sigh deeply. Reads as 'really sad' at A2+. Risk of collapse to 'sad'.
Mime: knock loudly on imaginary door, interrupt imaginary person reading by waving in their face, look apologetic. Reads at A2+. Risk of collapse to 'interrupt'.
Abstract noun (greatest work). Drawing 'famous painting + medal' reads as 'art'. Best: 'the best work of art or writing — Mona Lisa is a masterpiece'.
Function correlative phrase. Mime fails. Best: 'used to say two things are not true — neither pizza nor pasta is on the menu today'.
Mime: imaginary person speaks, then I think and respond with mouth moving + finger up. Reads at A2+ as 'answering'. Risk of collapse to 'speak'.
Specific abstract science noun. Drawing 'Earth surrounded by green ring of life' is plausible but vague. Best: 'parts of Earth where life exists — air, water, and land make up the biosphere'.

Specific abstract scientific concept. Drawing 'DNA helix + scissors' is plausible but specific to A2+ science learners. Best: 'changing the genes of living things — genetic engineering can make plants grow better'.
Mime: drop imaginary object from above, watch it fall, point at the floor. Reads at A2+ as 'gravity/falling'. Risk of collapse to 'fall'.
Abstract noun (useful thing). Drawing 'pile of various items + question mark' is too vague. Best: 'something useful you have — water is an important resource'.
Same as G3. Best: 'the outside or top part of something — the surface of the lake was calm'.
Abstract negative compound. Mime 'shake head + house with X' is too vague. Best: 'not suitable for living — Mars is uninhabitable for humans without a spacesuit'.
Specific role-noun. Drawing 'figure with badge + giving orders to others' reads at A2+ from media. Risk of collapse to 'soldier' or 'leader'.
Mime: do imaginary task with effort, slow down progressively, yawn, slump exhausted. Reads as 'making me tired' at A2+. Risk of collapse to 'tired'.
Set discourse phrase (sign-off). Mime 'wave + smile + hand on heart' is too vague. Best: 'a friendly phrase to end a letter — Best wishes, Anna'.

Abstract publishing noun. Drawing 'three different newspapers labelled 1st/2nd/3rd' is plausible but vague. Best: 'a particular version of a book or newspaper — this is the second edition of the book'.
Same as G2 'scuba diver' but as activity. Iconic visual — figure underwater with mask + tank + fins, bubbles rising. Drawing reads instantly.
Compound adjective. Drawing 'jacket with raindrops bouncing off' is plausible but vague. Best: 'not letting water in — my new watch is waterproof, I can swim with it'.
Mime: hold imaginary palette + brush, paint imaginary canvas with flair, step back to admire, wear imaginary beret. Reads at A2+ from cartoon. Risk of collapse to 'painter'.
Concrete object — signature with squiggle/flourish, often on photo or paper. Drawing reads at A2+. Risk of collapse to 'signature' — actor adds celebrity-photo framing.
Mime: lie back with hands behind head, feet up, deep relaxed breath, eyes closed with happy face. Universal at A2+ from many shared contexts.
Abstract relational adjective. Drawing 'two figures, one taller/older' reads as 'big' or 'old'. Best: 'older (especially of brothers/sisters) — my elder sister is 18'.

Polysemous (highlight a passage; the best moment; hair highlight). Per definition the 'best part' sense. Drawing 'star + thumbs up' is too vague. Best: 'the best part of something — the highlight of the trip was the beach'.
Set discourse phrase. Mime 'finger up + emphasise final point' is too vague. Best: 'a way to say the last thing is also important — Last but not least, thanks to my mum'.
Concrete location — large building with pool/gym/cafe icons. Drawing reads at A2+ from local context. Risk of collapse to 'gym'. Backup: actor adds the multi-activity icons.

rows.g: ab und zu; hin und wieder
rows.justification: Adverb of frequency. Mime 'shrug + raise hand 1-2 fingers' is too vague. Best: 'sometimes but not often — I occasionally eat sushi, maybe once a month'.
Specific abstract verb (formally ask). Mime 'hand over imaginary papers + cross fingers' is too vague. Best: 'formally ask for a job or course — I'm going to apply for the summer programme'.
Abstract trait-noun (self-control). Mime 'sit still with rigid posture + serious face' collapses to 'sitting'. Best: 'controlling yourself and working hard — sport requires discipline'.
Polysemous adverb (truthfully; really). Mime 'hand on heart + serious face' reads as 'honest' (the adjective). Best: 'truthfully — Honestly, I don't know the answer'.
Polysemous abstract adjective (difficult; physically strong; chewy meat). Mime 'flex muscle + tighten jaw' reads as 'strong'. Best: 'difficult, needing effort — that test was tough'.

Concrete competition format — bracket diagram with team names + lines, or trophy at the top. Drawing reads at A2+ from sport contexts. Risk of collapse to 'competition' — actor adds the bracket structure.

Iconic visual — figure sitting on street with cup or sign, ragged clothes. Drawing reads at A2+ but sensitive in classroom. Best handled compassionately. Backup: explain via 'a person who asks strangers for money'.
Concrete substance — black lumpy rocks, often piled or in a bucket. Iconic at A2+. Drawing reads instantly.
Polysemous (old story; famous person). Per definition the 'old story' sense. Drawing 'old book + dragon/knight' is too narrative. Best: 'an old well-known story — the legend of King Arthur'.

Concrete adjective applied to fruit. Drawing 'red apple + green apple side by side, red labelled OK to eat' captures the sense. Best in words to handle the abstract: 'ready to eat because it's fully grown — eat the banana when it's ripe'.
Idiomatic phrasal verb. Mime 'rush forward to catch up + open imaginary book' is plausible but vague. Best: 'do something you didn't have time for — I need to catch up on my homework'.
Idiomatic verb. Mime 'step into a circle of activity' is too vague. Best: 'become part of an activity — she got involved with the school newspaper'.
Mime: see imaginary person struggling with task, step forward, help carry something or fix problem. Reads at A2+. Risk of collapse to 'help'.

Idiomatic phrase. Mime 'check imaginary watch + look bored + scroll phone aimlessly' is plausible but reads as 'bored'. Best: 'do something to keep busy while waiting — I killed time at the airport by reading'.
Mime: count imaginary money fanned out, point at imaginary cash register, show satisfied 'cha-ching' face. Reads at A2+. Risk of collapse to 'money' or 'rich'.
Mime: pretend to look after imaginary baby/pet — feed, hold gently, comb hair, smile lovingly. Reads at A2+. Risk of collapse to 'baby' or 'pet'.

Polysemous phrasal verb (start a hobby; occupy space; raise). Per definition the 'start a hobby' sense. Mime 'hold up new instrument/sport-equipment with eager face' is plausible but specific. Best: 'start doing a new activity — I took up tennis last summer'.
Same as G3. Best: 'go to an event, school, or meeting — only ten people attended the meeting'.
